develop:0.en: Rain drums against the window as I sort the shelves. The Manager watches me arrange the drinks by size and nods slowly. 'You need to *develop* good habits early,' he says, handing me a checklist no one told me existed. I count fourteen items. I have done three.
develop:0.cnHint: 店长看着我整理货架，给了我一张从没人提起过的清单，说要尽早____好习惯。
develop:0.hook: The checklist has a fifteenth item, written in red.
develop:0.line: 'You need to *develop* good habits early, or the night shift will break you.'

level:0.en: The rain is heavy tonight. Tang shows me how to stack the instant noodle boxes — each row at the same *level*, edges perfectly straight. 'Customers notice,' she says, though no one has come in for an hour. Then the door opens and a soaked man walks straight to the noodles without looking up.
level:0.cnHint: 阿糖教我把货物摆到同一____，说顾客会注意到的，这时一个浑身湿透的男人推门而入。
level:0.hook: He picks up the same box three times, then puts it back.
level:0.line: 'Keep every row at the same *level* — trust me, it matters.'

enjoy:0.en: I pour myself a small cup of hot tea from the staff kettle and stand by the warm counter. For one quiet moment I actually *enjoy* the sound of rain on the roof and the soft hum of the fridges. Then I notice the old woman outside, standing still under a broken umbrella, staring at the door.
enjoy:0.cnHint: 我在柜台边____着雨声和冰箱的嗡嗡声，却发现门外有一位老太太一动不动地站在雨里。
enjoy:0.hook: She has been standing there for exactly twelve minutes.
enjoy:0.line: 'I *enjoy* the quiet nights — nothing bad ever happens on rainy nights.'

fact:0.en: A young man in a wet jacket buys one banana and pays with exact coins. Tang leans over and whispers, 'He comes every rainy night. Only ever buys one banana.' I ask why. She shrugs. 'That is the *fact*. Nobody knows the reason.' He pauses at the door and looks back at us.
fact:0.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我一个____：那个男人每个雨夜都来，只买一根香蕉，没有人知道原因。
fact:0.hook: He mouths something before stepping into the rain.
fact:0.line: 'That is just the *fact* — he always comes, and he never explains.'

news:0.en: The little TV above the door plays the late *news* on low volume. A woman hurries in, dripping wet, and freezes when she hears the presenter say a name. Her bag falls from her shoulder. She does not pick it up. She just stares at the screen with wide, still eyes.
news:0.cnHint: 电视里播放着深夜____，一个女人冲进来后突然停住，死死盯着屏幕。
news:0.hook: The name on the screen is the same as the one on her bag tag.
news:0.line: 'Turn the *news* up — I need to hear what they just said.'

company:0.en: It is nearly three in the morning and the rain has not stopped. I tell Tang I am fine alone, but she pulls up a stool anyway. 'On nights like this,' she says, 'the *company* matters more than the work.' We sit in easy silence. Then someone knocks on the glass from outside — not the door, the glass.
company:0.cnHint: 阿糖说雨夜里____比工作更重要，两人静静坐着，这时有人敲响了玻璃。
company:0.hook: There is no one visible outside when I look up.
company:0.line: 'On a night like this, the *company* is the only thing that keeps you sane.'

cost:0.en: The Manager calls from home to check the register. He asks if I gave the student a discount on her umbrella. I say yes — it was raining hard and she had no coins left. He is quiet for a moment. 'That *cost* us forty cents,' he says, then adds, 'Good call.' He hangs up before I can answer.
cost:0.cnHint: 店长打来电话，说我给那个学生打折让我们损失了四十分钱，然后说了一句奇怪的话就挂断了。
cost:0.hook: The student left something small on the counter when she went.
cost:0.line: 'That *cost* us forty cents — but I would have done the same thing.'

idea:0.en: The lights flicker once during the storm. Tang grabs a torch from under the counter without looking. I ask how she knew where it was. She smiles. 'The Manager had the *idea* to tape a torch there on my first night. Said the power goes out every summer.' I check under my side of the counter. There is a note instead.
idea:0.cnHint: 阿糖说店长在她第一个夜班就想到了把手电筒放在那里，我在我这边找到的却不是手电筒。
idea:0.hook: The note is dated three years ago and has my name on it.
idea:0.line: 'It was the Manager's *idea* — he thinks of everything before you even arrive.'

reduce:0.en: Rain hammered the roof all night. By three in the morning, the store had only two customers left. I turned off half the ceiling lights to *reduce* the electricity bill, just as the Manager had shown me. The soft glow made the shelves look almost cosy. Then the door opened.
reduce:0.cnHint: 深夜大雨，我按店长教的方法____了电费支出，就在这时门开了。
reduce:0.hook: A soaking-wet stranger stepped in, eyes wide with fear.
reduce:0.line: 'We always *reduce* the lights after midnight — house rules.'

process:0.en: Tang was teaching me the closing checklist. 'It is a long *process*,' she said, ticking boxes one by one — frozen goods, cash drawer, mop log. The rain outside grew louder with each step. We were halfway through when the phone behind the counter rang, sharp and sudden.
process:0.cnHint: 同事正耐心教我收摊的____，电话突然响了。
process:0.hook: Nobody called the store phone at three in the morning.
process:0.line: 'The whole *process* takes twenty minutes if you stay focused.'

able:0.en: The storm had knocked out the traffic lights on the corner. A delivery rider pushed his bike inside, soaked to the bone. He tried to dry his hands enough to be *able* to swipe his card for a hot drink. I quietly handed him a paper towel without being asked.
able:0.cnHint: 暴风雨中，外卖骑手努力让自己____刷卡买热饮。
able:0.hook: His phone buzzed — someone was still placing orders in this weather.
able:0.line: 'I was barely *able* to see the road out there.'

drive:0.en: Lin arrived just before four, shaking rain off her jacket. She ran the small shop two doors down and we were rivals, sort of. But the storm gave her no choice — the *drive* to stay open through the night had brought her here for coffee and a dry spot.
drive:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林被一股____迫使她冒雨来到这家便利店。
drive:0.hook: She set her coffee down and said, 'We need to talk.'
drive:0.line: 'Pure *drive* is the only thing keeping my shop open tonight.'

face:0.en: I was refilling the hot-food shelf when I noticed the small mirror above the register. My own *face* looked back at me — pale, tired, a little lost. Eight hours into my first night shift and I still had not learned where the spare bags were kept. Tang noticed and smiled.
face:0.cnHint: 我在镜子里看到自己疲惫的____，同事注意到了并微笑安慰我。
face:0.hook: Then Tang pointed at the shelf behind me and whispered, 'Look.'
face:0.line: 'Your *face* says you have not found the spare bags yet.'

possible:0.en: The rain showed no sign of stopping. I started wondering how it was *possible* that anyone would walk in at this hour. Then, within ten minutes, four people came through the door — a nurse, a student, a tired parent, and someone I could not quite place at all.
possible:0.cnHint: 我好奇这么晚____还有人来，结果十分钟内进来了四个陌生人。
possible:0.hook: The last one in wore a coat that was completely dry.
possible:0.line: 'Is it *possible* to get a warm meal at this hour?'

similar:0.en: The nurse bought the same thing every visit — rice ball, green tea, a small bar of chocolate. Tonight a young student picked out the exact *similar* set without knowing it. They ended up at the same counter at the same moment and looked at each other's basket with wide eyes.
similar:0.cnHint: 护士和学生不约而同选了____的东西，两人在柜台前面面相觑。
similar:0.hook: The nurse laughed softly and said one quiet sentence.
similar:0.line: 'We have *similar* taste — maybe that means something.'

involve:0.en: Tang pulled me aside and explained that the late shift could sometimes *involve* a bit of unofficial problem-solving — lost keys, missed buses, people who just needed somewhere warm to sit. 'The Manager never wrote that in the job notes,' she added, glancing at the door, 'but here we are.'
involve:0.cnHint: 同事告诉我，夜班工作有时会____一些规定之外的小事。
involve:0.hook: Outside, someone pressed their face against the wet glass.
involve:0.line: 'This job can *involve* more than just scanning barcodes.'

suggest:0.en: Rain tapped the window all evening. Around midnight, an old man stood at the door, soaking wet, holding nothing but a small paper bag. He looked at the umbrella stand near the counter and then at me. 'I *suggest* you keep more of those,' he said quietly, nodding at the last umbrella. Then he bought it and walked back into the dark.
suggest:0.cnHint: 一位深夜被雨淋湿的老人____我们多备些雨伞，然后买走了最后一把。
suggest:0.hook: He never once looked at the price tag.
suggest:0.line: 'I *suggest* you keep more of those near the door.'

improve:0.en: The Manager called during a slow, rainy hour to check on things. I told him sales were fine but the mop was falling apart. He laughed softly. 'We should *improve* the store little by little,' he said. 'Start with the mop.' After we hung up, I noticed a woman outside writing something in a small notebook, rain or no rain.
improve:0.cnHint: 店长打来电话，说要____小店的各种条件，我注意到门外有个女人在雨中记着什么。
improve:0.hook: She had been standing there for twenty minutes.
improve:0.line: 'We should *improve* things little by little, starting small.'

affect:0.en: A cold rain had been falling since nine. Tang arrived for the handover with wet shoes and a cheerful face. 'Don't let the weather *affect* your mood,' Tang said, shaking water from a jacket. 'Rainy nights are actually the best — people buy hot drinks and talk more.' Tang was right. By ten, the counter felt warmer than usual.
affect:0.cnHint: 同事阿糖说不要让坏天气____心情，雨夜其实顾客更爱聊天。
affect:0.hook: Tang had clearly learned that from someone specific.
affect:0.line: 'Don't let the rain *affect* your mood tonight.'

support:0.en: A tired-looking student came in just after eleven, dripping on the floor mat. She bought two rice balls and a hot tea, then sat on the small bench by the window. 'My friends gave me a lot of *support* before my exam,' she said to no one in particular, staring at the rain. She looked like the exam had not gone the way she hoped.
support:0.cnHint: 一个落汤鸡似的学生说朋友们给了她很多____，但她的表情让人觉得考试没发挥好。
support:0.hook: She ordered the same thing again an hour later.
support:0.line: 'Their *support* really kept me going through the whole week.'

hand:0.en: Just before one in the morning, a boy ran in from the rain holding a soaked cardboard box. 'Could you give me a *hand* with this?' he asked breathlessly, setting the box on the counter. Inside, wrapped in a dry cloth, was a small orange cat, fast asleep. He said he had found it under a bench three streets away.
hand:0.cnHint: 一个男孩冲进来请我帮____，纸箱里裹着一只他在街边捡到的熟睡小橘猫。
hand:0.hook: The cat opened one eye and looked directly at me.
hand:0.line: 'Could you give me a *hand* with this box, please?'

finding:0.en: Lin from the shop down the street came in around two, shaking rain off a hood. 'Interesting *finding*,' Lin said, leaning on the counter. 'Our hot food sales go up thirty percent on rainy nights. Yours?' I checked the screen. Ours were up forty. I smiled but said nothing. Lin tapped the counter once, nodded, and left without buying anything.
finding:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林分享了一个雨夜销售数据的____，我默默看了看自家的数字，只是微笑。
finding:0.hook: Lin paused at the door just a second too long.
finding:0.line: 'Interesting *finding* — our numbers go up every rainy night.'

ago:0.en: A woman in a yellow raincoat came in and went straight to the back shelf, reaching for a specific brand of crackers without looking. 'I used to work here,' she said when she caught me watching. 'Three years *ago*. Same shelf, same crackers.' She smiled at the shelf like it was an old friend, paid, and left. I checked the staff records after she was gone.
ago:0.cnHint: 一位穿黄雨衣的女士说她三年____曾在这里工作，我在她离开后悄悄翻了员工档案。
ago:0.hook: Her name was not in any of the records.
ago:0.line: 'I worked the night shift here three years *ago*.'

essay:0.en: Around three in the morning, a young man spread papers all over the window table and ordered four coffees one by one over two hours. On his third cup he looked up at me. 'I have to finish this *essay* before sunrise,' he said, with a smile that was equal parts tired and proud. The rain had softened to a whisper by then. I quietly turned down the music.
essay:0.cnHint: 一个男生在店里熬夜赶____，他的笑容一半是疲惫一半是自豪，我悄悄把音乐调小了。
essay:0.hook: He had written his conclusion first, then stopped.
essay:0.line: 'I have to finish this *essay* before the sun comes up.'

conversation:0.en: Rain tapped the window all night. Around 2 a.m., an old man came in, bought a hot tea, and sat by the heater. He started a *conversation* with me about nothing in particular — the rain, bad buses, the price of eggs. I mostly listened. By 3 a.m. he was gone, leaving only a wet umbrella by the door.
conversation:0.cnHint: 深夜，一位老人买了杯热茶，跟我展开了一段____，聊些鸡毛蒜皮的小事。
conversation:0.hook: He left the umbrella — but no one came back for it.
conversation:0.line: 'A good *conversation* on a rainy night is better than any medicine, kid.'

self:0.en: The rain kept everyone away until a young woman rushed in, soaking wet, and stood in front of the snack shelf for a long time. She seemed to be arguing with her *self*, picking up a bag of chips, putting it back, picking it up again. She bought the chips. And a salad. And two more bags of chips. I understood completely.
self:0.cnHint: 一个淋湿的女孩站在零食架前，似乎在和____纠结要不要买薯片。
self:0.hook: She paid and whispered something that sounded like a name.
self:0.line: 'I need to stop arguing with my *self* at two in the morning.'

age:0.en: Tang and I were quietly restocking shelves when an elderly woman shuffled in. She moved slowly but her eyes were sharp. She picked out green tea, paid exact change, and told me her *age* without my asking — eighty-one. Then she said she had walked here every rainy night for thirty years. The Manager had never mentioned her once.
age:0.cnHint: 一位老太太进来买茶，主动告诉我她的____，说她在雨夜来这里已经三十年了。
age:0.hook: She called the store by a name that was different from its sign.
age:0.line: 'At my *age*, a warm shop on a cold night is the whole world.'

future:0.en: A teenager sat on the step outside, under the small roof, staring at his phone. When the rain got heavier I waved him inside. He bought nothing, just stood there. He said he had just failed an important exam and could not think about the *future* right now. I handed him a free hot chocolate. Some problems need a pause, not a plan.
future:0.cnHint: 一个刚考砸的男孩站在店里，说他现在根本没法想____的事。
future:0.hook: He left the empty cup on the counter and wrote two words on a receipt.
future:0.line: 'I know I should think about the *future*, but tonight I just can not.'

effect:0.en: The Manager once told me that keeping the store warm and bright had a strong *effect* on late-night customers — they stayed longer and spent more. I thought he was just being clever. But tonight, watching four strangers quietly share a heater in the rain, I started to think he might actually be right. Or maybe they just liked the light.
effect:0.cnHint: 店长说温暖明亮的环境对深夜顾客有很大的____，今晚我似乎开始相信他的话了。
effect:0.hook: One of the four strangers left without paying — and left twice the amount on the counter.
effect:0.line: 'A warm light has a real *effect* on people, whether they know it or not.'

local:0.en: A man came in wearing a jacket from the *local* university. He bought three energy drinks and spread a map across the counter without asking. He was planning a cycling route around the city for Saturday. Tang leaned over to look and immediately started correcting the route with a pen. I did not know Tang cycled. I did not know Tang owned a pen.
local:0.cnHint: 一个穿着____大学外套的男人把地图摊在收银台上，同事唐凑过去帮他改路线。
local:0.hook: The man folded the map carefully and said he would be back Friday.
local:0.line: 'Every *local* knows that road floods after heavy rain — avoid it.'

tend:0.en: Lin from the store across the street came in just before dawn, as she sometimes does when her delivery is late. She *tends* to buy exactly one coffee and stand near the window, watching her own dark shop. She never stays long. Tonight she looked at me and said, 'Your light is brighter than mine.' I had no good answer for that.
tend:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林有时会在黎明前来买杯咖啡，她____会站在窗边望着自家黑暗的店铺。
tend:0.hook: She left a coin on the sill — the old kind, not used anymore.
tend:0.line: 'I *tend* to come here when the night feels too quiet across the street.'

term:0.en: A tired-looking student dropped a thick textbook on the counter and asked if we sold highlighters. We did not. She sighed and bought three pens instead. She said the whole *term* had been like this — always missing one small thing. She highlighted her notes with a red pen and a blue pen together. It looked like it worked fine to me.
term:0.cnHint: 一个学生抱怨整个____都不顺，总是缺少某样小东西，最后用两支普通笔将就过去了。
term:0.hook: She left the textbook behind — it had someone else's name inside the cover.
term:0.line: 'This whole *term* I have been solving problems with the wrong tools.'

risk:0.en: Rain hammers the roof. The last bus left an hour ago, and a delivery driver bursts through the door, soaking wet. He slides a soggy package onto the counter. 'I nearly dropped it in a puddle,' he says. I dry it with a cloth, wondering why anyone would *risk* a bicycle ride in this weather.
risk:0.cnHint: 一个快递员冒着大雨骑车来送货，我帮他擦干了包裹。
risk:0.hook: The address label reads the Manager's name.
risk:0.line: 'Why would you *risk* cycling in a storm like this?'

success:0.en: The Manager pins a small paper sign above the register: 'One year open — thank you!' She tells me the first month was so slow she ate instant noodles every night. Now the shelves are nearly empty by dawn. She smiles at the sign, and I realise quiet *success* can look exactly like a warm, well-lit room on a rainy street.
success:0.cnHint: 店长讲起便利店艰难起步的故事，感叹如今终于____.
success:0.hook: Then her phone buzzes — and her smile fades.
success:0.line: 'Real *success* is still standing after that first terrible month.'

group:0.en: Just after midnight, a *group* of four students tumble in from the rain, laughing and shaking water off their jackets. They argue happily over which flavour of rice ball is best. They spread their books across the two small tables near the window, turning the quiet store into something that feels like a library.
group:0.cnHint: 深夜，一群学生跑进来避雨，把便利店变成了临时自习室。
group:0.hook: One of them keeps glancing at the door, waiting for someone.
group:0.line: 'Our whole study *group* needed somewhere dry tonight.'

course:0.en: Tang explains the shop routine to me between customers. 'Of *course* you always face the labels outward,' she says, straightening a row of canned drinks with one finger. She makes it sound obvious, but I have already turned three cans the wrong way tonight. Outside, rain slides down the glass in long, crooked lines.
course:0.cnHint: 同事耐心教我整理货架，说这些规矩____是理所当然的。
course:0.hook: She suddenly lowers her voice — the Manager is watching.
course:0.line: 'Of *course* the labels face out — first rule of this store.'

relationship:0.en: A regular, an older man with an umbrella, buys the same warm milk tea every night. Tonight he lingers, turning his cup slowly. 'My daughter and I barely talk,' he says quietly, almost to himself. He leaves before I can reply. I wonder how a small cup of tea fits into a *relationship* that seems to have very few words left in it.
relationship:0.cnHint: 一位老常客提起自己与女儿的____，言语间透着遗憾。
relationship:0.hook: He leaves his change on the counter — every last coin.
relationship:0.line: 'A *relationship* takes time, but silence takes it faster.'

form:0.en: A woman rushes in holding a damp envelope. She needs to fill in a *form* for a night-school application, and her pen has run dry. I lend her one from the drawer under the register. She writes quickly, pressing hard, her hand trembling slightly. Rain taps the window like it is also impatient for her answer.
form:0.cnHint: 一位女士冒雨跑来，急着填一份____，向我借了笔。
form:0.hook: The deadline printed on the form is tonight at midnight.
form:0.line: 'Do you have a pen? I must finish this *form* now.'

interest:0.en: Lin from the shop across the street ducks in, pretending to browse. She picks up a small potted cactus we sell near the door and studies it with great *interest*. I know she is really checking our new display of hot drinks. I straighten the cans slowly and say nothing. We are rivals, but tonight the rain makes enemies feel more like neighbours.
interest:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林假装对一盆仙人掌很有____，其实在偷看我们的新品。
interest:0.hook: She takes a photo — then notices I am watching.
interest:0.line: 'I just have a little *interest* in your new drinks shelf.'

simply:0.en: At three in the morning the rain finally slows to a whisper. The store is empty and very still. I wipe the counter and look at the wet street outside. I thought this job would be boring, but tonight brought a delivery driver, a study group, a sad father, and a rival. I *simply* did not expect a night shift to feel this full.
simply:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点，雨渐渐停了，我____没想到夜班会有这么多故事。
simply:0.hook: Then the phone behind the counter rings — at 3 a.m.
simply:0.line: 'I *simply* cannot believe how much happens in one night here.'

put:0.en: Rain hammered the roof. I *put* a small paper cup under the drip by the freezer, then slid a wet-floor sign next to it. The Manager watched from the door of the back room, arms crossed. He said nothing, but the corner of his mouth moved — just once.
put:0.cnHint: 我把纸杯____在漏水处，店长默默看着。
put:0.hook: The Manager picked up the cup and walked to the back room.
put:0.line: '*Put* that sign closer to the door, or someone will slip.'

difference:0.en: Tang had worked nights here for two years. I had worked nights here for two weeks. You would think there was a big *difference* between us. But when the rain came in hard and we both grabbed mops without a word, I felt the gap close to almost nothing.
difference:0.cnHint: 我和阿糖之间的____，在大雨来临时似乎消失了。
difference:0.hook: Tang glanced at me and said, 'Not bad for two weeks.'

lack:0.en: The shelves near the window looked thin. I checked the list and found a clear *lack* of hot drinks — only two cans of milk tea left. Outside, rain-soaked students were already crossing the street toward us, hoods up, looking cold and hopeful.
lack:0.cnHint: 货架上热饮____，一群淋湿的学生正朝店里走来。
lack:0.hook: The first student pushed open the door and grabbed both cans.

case:0.en: A woman in a yellow raincoat stepped in, carrying a hard plastic *case* the size of a shoe box. She set it on the counter, peeled off her wet gloves, and asked for a hot coffee. The case had small air holes in the sides. Something inside it moved.
case:0.cnHint: 一位女士带着一个有气孔的____走进来，里面有动静。
case:0.hook: She pressed one finger gently against an air hole and whispered.

sure:0.en: I was not *sure* the umbrella stand by the door was my job to empty. Water was pooling on the floor. I looked at Tang. Tang looked at the ceiling. The Manager looked at me. I emptied the stand. Apparently, it was my job.
sure:0.cnHint: 我不____伞架该不该我来处理，结果店长的眼神给了我答案。
sure:0.hook: Tang smiled and handed me a dry cloth without being asked.

enough:0.en: By midnight the rain had not stopped. We had sold *enough* hot soup cups to clear the whole rack, and the coin tray was satisfyingly heavy. I refilled the rack. The street outside was empty except for one figure standing still under a broken street lamp.
enough:0.cnHint: 热汤卖得很好，____让货架见了底，但窗外有个人一动不动。
enough:0.hook: The figure had been standing there for twenty minutes.

attention:0.en: Lin came in from next door during a quiet gap in the rain. She did not buy anything. She walked slowly along our snack wall, paying careful *attention* to every price tag. I pretended to restock the gum rack and paid careful attention right back.
attention:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林仔细打量我们的价签，我则假装整理货架，把____都放在她身上。
attention:0.hook: Lin took a photo of our lowest price and left without a word.

certain:0.en: A *certain* regular — I still did not know his name — came in at exactly 2 a.m. as he always did. He bought one rice ball and one small coffee, same as every night. Tonight he also bought a single birthday candle. He asked me not to mention it.
certain:0.cnHint: 某位熟客今晚多买了一根生日蜡烛，还叮嘱我____事不要说出去。
certain:0.hook: He left quickly, and the rain outside seemed to soften for him.

popular:0.en: Rain hammers the roof. I arrange a fresh display near the door — hot drinks, dry snacks, small umbrellas. Tang watches me and nods. 'Umbrellas are always *popular* on rainy nights,' she says. By nine o'clock, the little stand is nearly empty. Someone left a wet note beside the last one.
popular:0.cnHint: 雨夜里，某样商品格外____，货架很快就空了，还留下一张神秘的纸条。
popular:0.hook: The wet note had no name, only three words.
popular:0.line: 'Umbrellas are always *popular* on rainy nights,' Tang says with a knowing smile.

current:0.en: The Manager pins a hand-written sign above the register. I lean in to read it. 'Please check the *current* price list — everything changed at midnight.' Rain taps the window. A regular pushes through the door, shaking water off his coat, and stares at the sign for a long moment.
current:0.cnHint: 店长贴出通知，说明____的价格表已经更新，一位常客看后表情很奇怪。
current:0.hook: He pulled out an old receipt and said nothing.
current:0.line: 'Please check the *current* price list before you pay,' the Manager says quietly.

difficult:0.en: A woman rushes in, soaking wet, and tries to read the map on her phone with shaking hands. Finding the right bus stop is *difficult* in heavy rain with a dead battery warning. I draw a small map on a paper bag and slide it across the counter. She stares at it.
difficult:0.cnHint: 一位浑身湿透的女士觉得找公交站____，我用纸袋画了一张地图递给她。
difficult:0.hook: She looked at my drawing, then at me, and laughed once.
difficult:0.line: 'Everything is so *difficult* when the rain will not stop,' she says softly.

amount:0.en: I count the coins in the small charity box near the door. The *amount* surprises me — almost sixty yuan, all added tonight while rain fell outside. Tang comes over, peers into the box, and raises her eyebrows. A child's drawing is folded and tucked beneath the coins.
amount:0.cnHint: 我清点门口慈善箱里的零钱，今晚募集的____让大家都很惊讶，里面还藏着一幅画。
amount:0.hook: No one had seen who left the drawing.
amount:0.line: 'That *amount* came in only one rainy night,' Tang says, clearly surprised.

point:0.en: Lin slides a new product catalogue across the counter toward me. 'Read it. There will be a test.' I flip through the pages, lost, until she taps one paragraph. 'That is the *point* — the store's whole new direction.' Outside, rain washes the empty street clean and bright.
point:0.cnHint: 林递来新产品目录，指出文件中最关键的____，暗示店里将有大变化。
point:0.hook: The new direction meant one familiar item would disappear.
point:0.line: 'That is the *point* you need to remember before tomorrow,' Lin says firmly.

role:0.en: The Manager calls a quick meeting at the back of the store. Rain drums on the skylight above us. He explains that each of us has a clear *role* during the busy midnight rush: Tang handles the register, Lin manages the stock room, and I cover the door. Simple enough — or so I think.
role:0.cnHint: 店长开了个简短会议，说明每个人在午夜高峰时段扮演的____，听起来很简单。
role:0.hook: Then he told us who the mystery midnight regular really was.
role:0.line: 'Your *role* tonight is to watch the door carefully,' the Manager tells me.

survey:0.en: The rain drummed on the roof as I tried to *survey* the store for anything out of place. Wet footprints led from the door to the snack aisle, then stopped. Nobody was there. Tang leaned over the counter and whispered, 'Someone came in, grabbed nothing, and left. Third time this week.'
survey:0.cnHint: 深夜大雨，我仔细____着店内，发现湿漉漉的脚印突然消失了。
survey:0.hook: The footprints stopped right where the security camera had gone dark.
survey:0.line: 'Let's *survey* every corner before we close up tonight.'

care:0.en: Outside, the rain was heavy. A man in a thin jacket hurried in, cradling a small cardboard box with great *care*. He set it gently on the counter and asked for some warm water. Inside the box, something tiny moved. Tang handed over the water without a word.
care:0.cnHint: 一个男人冒雨跑进店里，小心翼翼地____着一个纸箱，向我们要热水。
care:0.hook: Whatever was inside that box made a sound none of us expected.
care:0.line: 'Please, handle it with *care* — it has not eaten today.'

state:0.en: By midnight the rain had not stopped. Tang stared at the ceiling, clearly in some far-off *state* of mind. I waved a hand in front of his face. Nothing. Then the phone behind the counter rang — a sound so sudden that we both jumped, knocking over a whole stand of pens.
state:0.cnHint: 唐盯着天花板，进入了某种出神的____，直到电话铃声把我们俩都吓了一跳。
state:0.hook: The caller asked for someone who had not worked here in years.
state:0.line: 'Sorry — I was in a strange *state*; what did the caller say?'

impact:0.en: The Manager arrived soaking wet and dropped a thick folder on the counter. 'New display plan,' he said, out of breath. 'The *impact* of last month's poor sales has to stop.' He spread the papers everywhere, knocking over my cold coffee. Tang hid a smile behind a broom.
impact:0.cnHint: 店长冲进来，说上个月糟糕的销售额造成的____必须扭转，随手打翻了我的咖啡。
impact:0.hook: Hidden inside the folder was a handwritten note addressed to Tang.
impact:0.line: 'The *impact* of this rain on our sales is already bad enough.'

reason:0.en: Around two in the morning, Lin walked in from across the street, shaking water off an umbrella. She bought nothing, just stood by the warm drinks shelf. I asked if she needed help. She gave a small shrug. 'No *reason* in particular,' she said. 'It is just too quiet over there alone.'
reason:0.cnHint: 凌晨两点，林走进来在货架旁站着，说自己来这里没有什么特别的____。
reason:0.hook: But her eyes kept drifting toward the telephone on the wall.
reason:0.line: 'There is every *reason* to stay inside on a night like this.'

close:0.en: The rain grew softer near dawn. Tang pulled two stools up to the counter and handed me a warm canned drink. We sat in easy silence, listening to water drip from the roof. It felt *close*, the way things do when you share a long quiet night with someone without trying.
close:0.cnHint: 快天亮时，我和唐坐在柜台前，无声相伴，有一种说不清的____感。
close:0.hook: Then his phone lit up, and the name on the screen made him flinch.
close:0.line: 'Working nights makes you *close* to people faster than you think.'

individual:0.en: A delivery worker pushed in, soaked through, and sorted six small packages on the floor. Each had a sticky note with a name. 'Every *individual* order, same building, same floor,' he muttered, baffled. 'Why not just shop together?' I offered him a paper towel. He looked at me like I had solved something.
individual:0.cnHint: 一个快递员把六个____包裹摆在地板上，搞不懂同一栋楼的人为什么不一起下单。
individual:0.hook: One of the packages was addressed simply to 'the night clerk.'
individual:0.line: 'Each *individual* box goes to a different name, but the same door.'

area:0.en: The Manager called just after three to ask how the new drinks were selling in the cold *area* near the door. I looked. Three cans were gone, replaced by a neat puddle of rainwater someone had dripped in. 'Selling fine,' I said. He paused, then asked, 'Do you hear dripping?'
area:0.cnHint: 店长打电话询问门口冷藏____的新饮料销量，我看过去才发现地上有一滩雨水。
area:0.hook: Behind the cold shelf, something small and dry was carefully hidden.
area:0.line: 'Keep that *area* by the door dry — customers keep slipping tonight.'

enable:0.en: Rain drums against the store windows all night. The Manager installed a small roof over the entrance last week. 'It will *enable* customers to stay dry while they search for their keys,' he told me proudly. He spent three hours on a ladder doing it himself. I wonder if he ever goes home.
enable:0.cnHint: 店长在入口处装了个小雨棚，____顾客找钥匙时不被淋湿。
enable:0.hook: But tonight, someone stands under it for a very long time.
enable:0.line: A dry entrance will *enable* people to come in, even on the worst nights.

simple:0.en: Tang taught me the closing checklist on my first night. 'It looks long,' she said, 'but the idea is *simple* — leave every shelf the way you would want to find it.' She said it so quietly, like a small secret. I wrote it in my notebook. Now I say it to myself every shift.
simple:0.cnHint: 阿糖教我说，整理货架的道理其实很____。
simple:0.hook: She has a second notebook she never lets anyone read.
simple:0.line: The rule is *simple*: treat every shelf like it belongs to you.

several:0.en: A tall man in a yellow raincoat came in and stood in the snack aisle for a long time. He picked up *several* bags of chips, read the back of each one carefully, then put them all down and bought nothing. He nodded at me on his way out. I nodded back. Rain is strange like that.
several:0.cnHint: 一个穿黄雨衣的男人拿起了____袋薯片，最后却什么都没买。
several:0.hook: He came back exactly one hour later with a small notebook.
several:0.line: I looked at *several* options, but none of them felt right tonight.

struggle:0.en: The printer behind the counter jams every night around two in the morning. Tonight I watched Tang deal with it — her hands calm, her face steady. 'Everyone has a *struggle* they hide well,' she said without looking up. I was not sure if she meant the printer. The receipt finally printed at 2:41.
struggle:0.cnHint: 阿糖一边修打印机，一边说每个人都有隐藏的____。
struggle:0.hook: Then her phone buzzed and her calm face changed completely.
struggle:0.line: The real *struggle* is not the machine — it is staying patient with it.

decision:0.en: Lin came in from the rain holding two umbrellas. 'I made a *decision*,' she announced to no one in particular, shaking water onto the floor mat. 'I will always carry a spare.' She bought a cup of warm soup and left one umbrella leaning against the counter. It is still there.
decision:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林进门宣布自己做了一个____，还把一把伞留在了柜台边。
decision:0.hook: The name written on the umbrella handle is not hers.
decision:0.line: It was a hard *decision*, but I think carrying two is just smart.

kid:0.en: A small boy ran in ahead of his grandmother, heading straight for the candy shelf. 'That *kid* could find chocolate in a dark room,' his grandmother said, laughing softly. She bought him one small piece and herself a warm tea. He held her hand all the way out. The store felt warmer after they left.
kid:0.cnHint: 一个小____冲进店里直奔糖果架，奶奶笑着跟在后面。
kid:0.hook: The grandmother paused at the door and looked back at me oddly.
kid:0.line: Any *kid* who walks in from the rain deserves at least one warm thing.

ability:0.en: The Manager can guess what a customer needs before they ask. He calls it nothing special, but Tang calls it a gift. 'His *ability* to read people built this store,' she told me while we restocked the shelves. I watched him guide an old man to the right medicine shelf without a word. I want to learn that.
ability:0.cnHint: 阿糖说店长____顾客心思的____是一种天赋，造就了这家店。
ability:0.hook: But the old man left something on the counter that the Manager stared at for a long time.
ability:0.line: His *ability* to make people feel welcome is why they always come back.

task:0.en: My *task* for the slow hours is to restock the top shelf — the one that needs the small step-stool. Tang warned me it wobbles. She was not wrong. I finished it, though, and stood back to look at the neat row of cans. Outside, the rain had stopped. The street was silver and quiet. Then the door opened.
task:0.cnHint: 我的____是补货，但那个小凳子晃晃悠悠让人捏了把汗。
task:0.hook: The person who walked in was soaking wet and looking for something specific.
task:0.line: The last *task* of the night always feels like the longest one.

develop:1.en: Rain drums on the shop roof all night. I step outside to check the drain and find a young woman in a yellow coat sketching the wet street under a small lamp. She says she wants to *develop* her drawing skills before graduation. Her pencil moves fast, catching the light on every puddle.
develop:1.cnHint: 一位女生在雨中用素描____她的绘画技巧。
develop:1.hook: Her sketchbook holds one page she will not show anyone.
develop:1.line: 'I need to *develop* this habit before the term ends,' she says.

level:1.en: The rain makes the old street slope look like a shallow river. I watch a delivery rider stop his bike and test the water with one boot. He shakes his head — the *level* is already above the kerb. He calls someone, looks worried, then spots our store light and rides slowly toward it.
level:1.cnHint: 骑手担心路面积水的____已经超过路缘石。
level:1.hook: Whatever he is carrying, it cannot get wet.
level:1.line: 'The water *level* is too high — I have to stop here,' he says.

enjoy:1.en: Old Mr. Tang — not my colleague, just a regular — sits on a dry step under our shop awning and opens a paper bag. He pulls out a warm meat bun and sighs with real pleasure. 'I *enjoy* rainy nights,' he tells me through the open door. 'Everyone else stays home, so the street is all mine.'
enjoy:1.cnHint: 一位老先生在雨夜的屋檐下____着属于自己的宁静。
enjoy:1.hook: He then mentions a name that makes the Manager go pale.
enjoy:1.line: 'I truly *enjoy* the quiet that rain brings,' he says softly.

fact:1.en: A woman runs in shaking water off her umbrella. She buys three energy drinks and lines them on the counter. I ask if she is studying late. She laughs and says the *fact* is she has not slept in two days — her team's app launch is tomorrow and the server is still broken.
fact:1.cnHint: 她坦白说，____是她已经两天没睡了。
fact:1.hook: She glances at her phone and her smile disappears.
fact:1.line: 'The *fact* is, we might not launch at all tonight,' she admits.

news:1.en: Lin rushes in from the rain, collar soaked, eyes bright. She worked the morning shift but came back for something. She grabs my arm and whispers that the *news* just broke — the building across the street has been sold and a big chain store is moving in next month. We both look at the Manager's door.
news:1.cnHint: 林匆忙赶来，带来了对面楼被卖掉的____。
news:1.hook: The light under the Manager's door stays on all night.
news:1.line: 'Have you heard the *news* about the building across the road?' Lin asks.

company:1.en: A teenager stands outside in the rain, phone pressed to his ear, not moving. I bring him a free cup of hot tea. He looks surprised. 'My grandmother hates being alone during storms,' he says. 'I stay on the call so she has some *company*.' He stands there another hour, talking softly.
company:1.cnHint: 少年在雨中打电话，只是为了给奶奶提供____。
company:1.hook: When he finally hangs up, his eyes are a little red.
company:1.line: 'She just needs some *company* when the thunder gets loud,' he says.

cost:1.en: A man in a suit bursts through the door asking for a pen and paper — his phone is dead. He scribbles numbers fast, muttering to himself. I catch one line: the *cost* of the flood damage to his small shop down the road is more than he can pay this month. He stares at the paper for a long time.
cost:1.cnHint: 他算出雨水对小店造成的损失____远超他的承受范围。
cost:1.hook: He folds the paper, puts it in his pocket, and almost smiles.
cost:1.line: 'The *cost* is higher than I thought — but I'll manage,' he murmurs.

idea:1.en: I find a soaked notebook on the step outside. Inside, someone has filled ten pages with sketches of our store — the sign, the drink fridge, the late-night regulars. At the top of the first page: 'a short film *idea*'. The drawings are careful and full of small funny details I had never noticed about my own workplace.
idea:1.cnHint: 一本被雨淋湿的笔记本里，装着关于便利店的短片____。
idea:1.hook: The last sketch is a face — and it looks exactly like mine.
idea:1.line: 'It started as a small *idea*, but now it feels like something real,' a voice says.

suggest:1.en: Rain taps the window like a shy visitor. A woman in a yellow coat stops outside, staring at our store sign. I step to the door. 'Come in — you look soaked,' I say. She smiles and points at the shop across the street. 'I wanted to *suggest* you put up a bigger sign. I almost missed you.' She walks in anyway.
suggest:1.cnHint: 一位穿黄色雨衣的女士站在门外，想对我们的招牌____一些意见。
suggest:1.hook: She knew the Manager's name before I even said it.
suggest:1.line: 'I wanted to *suggest* you put up a bigger sign — I almost missed you.'

improve:1.en: The rain is heavy tonight. Tang mops the wet floor near the door for the third time, sighing. 'We should *improve* the mat system,' Tang says, wringing out the mop. I nod and place a second mat down. A customer walks in, looks at the mats, and leaves a small muddy boot print right between them. Tang sighs again.
improve:1.cnHint: 唐拖了三遍地，觉得门口的防滑垫系统需要____。
improve:1.hook: The next customer who walked in was carrying an umbrella — and a very large dog.
improve:1.line: 'We should really *improve* the mat system before the whole floor turns into a lake.'

affect:1.en: Outside, the rain falls in sheets. A man in a suit stands under the narrow roof edge, checking his phone every few seconds. He steps in, water dripping from his sleeve. 'Does the rain *affect* the delivery time here?' he asks, eyeing the hot food shelf. His voice is calm but his hands are not.
affect:1.cnHint: 一位穿西装的男士走进来，问大雨是否会____今晚的配送时间。
affect:1.hook: His phone buzzed three times, and each time he looked more relieved.
affect:1.line: 'Does heavy rain *affect* your delivery times tonight?'

support:1.en: The Manager called during the slow hour. 'How is the new night shift?' The question felt warm, not like a check-up. I told him about the leaky roof corner and the missing price tag on the rice crackers. He laughed. 'I will send Tang tomorrow. You have my full *support*.' I hung up feeling less alone in the quiet store.
support:1.cnHint: 店长打来电话，告诉我有他的全力____，让我安心上夜班。
support:1.hook: Tang arrived the next evening with a ladder, a toolbox, and a very long list of other things to fix.
support:1.line: 'You have my full *support* — call me any time tonight.'

hand:1.en: A girl rushes in from the rain, homework papers tucked under her arm, ink already bleeding at the corners. She spreads them on the counter with a small groan. I reach across and offer her a dry cloth. 'Give me a *hand* with these?' she asks, looking up with hopeful eyes. I help her sort the dry pages from the wet ones.
hand:1.cnHint: 一个女孩冲进来，请求我帮她____救一救被雨淋湿的作业。
hand:1.hook: One of the wet pages was a letter, not homework at all.
hand:1.line: 'Could you give me a *hand* sorting these before the ink runs any more?'

finding:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street dashes in, shaking rain off his jacket. He leans on the counter with a grin. 'Interesting *finding*,' he says, pulling out his phone to show a local review. Someone had written that our store smells like fresh bread at midnight. We do not sell bread. Lin raises one eyebrow.
finding:1.cnHint: 林冲进来，分享了一个关于我们店的有趣____，让我们都很困惑。
finding:1.hook: We checked every shelf twice and never found the source of the smell.
finding:1.line: 'Interesting *finding* — someone says your store smells like fresh bread at midnight.'

ago:1.en: The rain woke something in the old neighbourhood. A man in his sixties pushes the door open slowly, looking around as if reading a room he once knew. 'I used to come here years *ago*,' he says softly, touching the edge of the candy shelf. 'Different owner, same corner.' He buys a single pack of mints and stands very still before leaving.
ago:1.cnHint: 一位老人走进来，说他多年____曾经常来这家店。
ago:1.hook: He left a folded note under the mint pack that I found only after he was gone.
ago:1.line: 'I used to stop here every night, years *ago*, after my late shift.'

essay:1.en: A student drops into the store just before midnight, rain-damp and wide-eyed. She sets her notebook on the counter and asks if she can stand there and think. 'My *essay* is due at eight,' she says, tapping her pen against her chin. I slide her a hot cup of tea without a word. She writes three lines, then stops and stares at the rain.
essay:1.cnHint: 一名学生深夜冲进来，说她的____明早就要交了，请求在柜台旁边想一想。
essay:1.hook: The three lines she wrote turned out to be in the wrong language entirely.
essay:1.line: 'My *essay* is due at eight and I have not written a single sentence yet.'

conversation:1.en: Rain drums on the glass door as I mop the wet floor near the entrance. An old man steps in, shaking water from his coat, and starts a *conversation* with me about whether the rain will stop before dawn. He speaks slowly, kindly, as if we have all the time in the world. We probably do — it is two in the morning.
conversation:1.cnHint: 一位老人深夜进店，和店员展开了一段关于雨天的____。
conversation:1.hook: He never bought anything, but he left his umbrella behind.
conversation:1.line: 'A good *conversation* is better than any medicine on a rainy night,' he said softly.

self:1.en: Tang warned me before my first shift: the night changes a person. Standing alone under the bright store lights while rain falls outside, I start to understand. There is nothing to do but face your *self* — your small worries, your quiet hopes. I rearrange the snack shelf for the third time just to feel useful.
self:1.cnHint: 夜班独处让店员开始直面内心深处的____。
self:1.hook: Then the door opened, and a soaking-wet figure rushed in.
self:1.line: 'You really learn about your *self* when the whole street is asleep,' Tang told me.

age:1.en: A woman with silver hair buys warm milk every night at exactly 2 a.m. The Manager told me her name once but I forgot. She moves with the careful grace that comes with *age*, never rushing, always smiling. Tonight she pats my hand and says I remind her of someone. I wonder who.
age:1.cnHint: 一位上了____的常客每晚定时来买热牛奶，让店员心生好奇。
age:1.hook: She paid with an old coin I had never seen before.
age:1.line: 'At my *age*, warm milk and a quiet street are all I need,' she said.

future:1.en: Lin from the store across the street ducks in out of the rain, dripping on my clean floor. We are supposed to be rivals, but at 3 a.m. rivalry feels silly. We talk about the *future* — whether either of us will still be working night shifts in five years. The rain gets louder. Neither of us has an answer.
future:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林深夜避雨，两人聊起了各自的____。
future:1.hook: Lin paused, then asked if I had ever thought about leaving this town.
future:1.line: 'Honestly, I have no idea what the *future* looks like from here,' Lin said.

effect:1.en: The Manager put a small speaker near the door last week. Soft piano music plays all night. I was not sure it would help, but the *effect* on tired customers is clear — they slow down, breathe out, stop looking at their phones. A delivery rider who usually grabs his drink and runs actually stayed to listen for a full minute tonight.
effect:1.cnHint: 店长放的轻音乐对深夜顾客产生了意想不到的____。
effect:1.hook: The rider set down his bag and closed his eyes.
effect:1.line: 'I did not expect this *effect* — I just wanted something to fill the silence,' the Manager said.

local:1.en: A man in a damp jacket buys two rice balls and tells me he writes for a *local* paper. Nobody reads it much, he says, but somebody has to keep track of small streets and quiet corners. He scribbles something in a notebook while he eats, glancing up at the rain-soaked window now and then.
local:1.cnHint: 一位为____报纸写稿的男人在雨夜来买饭团，引起了店员的好奇。
local:1.hook: He tore a page from his notebook and tucked it under the counter without a word.
local:1.line: 'The *local* stories are the ones that actually matter,' he said between bites.

tend:1.en: I notice that customers who come in after 2 a.m. *tend* to buy one of three things: warm drinks, instant noodles, or chocolate. Tang says it is loneliness more than hunger. A young woman tonight bought all three, lined them up on the counter, and stared at them for a moment before laughing quietly at herself.
tend:1.cnHint: 深夜顾客____于购买某几类商品，让人忍不住猜测背后的原因。
tend:1.hook: She left one bar of chocolate on the counter — for me, she said.
tend:1.line: 'Night-shift people *tend* to understand each other without many words,' Tang once told me.

term:1.en: A student bursts in out of the rain, school bag soaking wet. She buys three energy drinks and stacks her notes on my counter to study. She tells me her exam is tomorrow — the last one of the *term*. She has been awake since yesterday. Her handwriting is still very neat, which impresses me more than I can say.
term:1.cnHint: 一名学生在____末考试前夜冒雨来店里买饮料备考。
term:1.hook: She left one page of notes behind, and the top question was circled in red.
term:1.line: 'If I pass this exam, I am sleeping for the whole next *term*,' she declared.

reduce:1.en: Rain hammers the street outside. I dash from the bus stop to the store, soaked to the skin. The Manager hands me a dry cloth and a warm cup without a word. 'Keeping an umbrella by the door will *reduce* the damage next time,' he says, nodding at the puddle I left on the tiles.
reduce:1.cnHint: 大雨中，店长教我如何____下班途中被淋湿的狼狈。
reduce:1.hook: He already had a spare umbrella waiting — with my name taped to the handle.
reduce:1.line: 'Keeping an umbrella by the door will *reduce* the damage next time.'

process:1.en: Tang explains the closing routine while rain taps the window. Count the cash, log the receipts, restock the cold drinks. 'The whole *process* takes about twenty minutes if nothing goes wrong,' she says, ticking each step off on her fingers. Nothing went wrong — until the register jammed on the very last receipt.
process:1.cnHint: 阿糖向我介绍收摊的____，直到收银机在最后一步出了故障。
process:1.hook: Tang's smile stayed calm — which meant she had seen this before.
process:1.line: 'The whole *process* takes about twenty minutes if nothing goes wrong.'

able:1.en: A delivery truck blocks the corner, and rain turns the road into a small river. I worry our morning bread order will be late. Then I spot the driver wading toward us, box held high above his head. 'I was barely *able* to get through,' he says, laughing as water drips from his jacket onto the floor.
able:1.cnHint: 大雨让街角变成了小河，送货员几乎无法____穿越积水送来早班面包。
able:1.hook: He pulled a second, sealed box from under his coat — no one had ordered it.
able:1.line: 'I was barely *able* to get through, but here I am!'

drive:1.en: The rain eases just after midnight. An old man parks a bicycle — not a car — under our awning and walks in slowly. I wonder what could *drive* someone out in weather like this. He picks up one small bottle of cough medicine, pays with exact change, and turns without a word toward the dark street.
drive:1.cnHint: 深夜的一场雨后，某种____促使一位老人冒雨出来买一瓶止咳药。
drive:1.hook: The bicycle had a child's seat on the back.
drive:1.line: 'Only love can *drive* a person out on a night like this, I think.'

face:1.en: Lin appears in the doorway, rain dripping from their hair, holding two cups of hot tea from the cafe next door. 'Peace offering,' Lin says with a grin. I look at the *face* of the clock above the door — it is three in the morning — and wonder how long our stores have really been rivals.
face:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜冒雨送来热茶，我看了一眼时钟的____，开始重新思考两家店的关系。
face:1.hook: Lin stayed to help me restock the shelves without being asked.
face:1.line: 'Look at the *face* of that clock — three in the morning and I am still here.'

possible:1.en: The rain brings a power flicker, and half the lights go out. I grab a torch and check the back room. The Manager calls from home: 'Is it *possible* the fuse box tripped again? Check the grey panel near the mop bucket.' I find the panel, flip the switch, and the store floods with warm light.
possible:1.cnHint: 停电后，店长打来电话，问我是否____是保险丝盒又跳闸了。
possible:1.hook: Behind the grey panel, someone had taped a hand-drawn map of the whole store.
possible:1.line: 'Is it *possible* the fuse box tripped? Check the grey panel.'

similar:1.en: A young woman rushes in out of the rain and grabs an umbrella from the stand. She holds it next to another one and frowns. 'They look so *similar* — which one is stronger?' I check the labels and hand her the sturdier one. She smiles, pays, and runs back into the storm without another word.
similar:1.cnHint: 一位女顾客比较两把雨伞，因为它们外观太____，难以区分哪把更结实。
similar:1.hook: She left a folded note on the counter — it was a weather forecast for the whole week.
similar:1.line: 'They look so *similar* — how do I know which one will last?'

involve:1.en: The Manager leaves a note on the counter before I start my shift. It says the morning audit will *involve* counting every item in aisle three by hand, because three bags of rice have gone missing in a week. I stare at the long shelf and sigh. Then Tang walks in early, rolling up her sleeves.
involve:1.cnHint: 店长留言说早上的盘点将____逐一清点第三排货架，因为一周内三袋米离奇失踪。
involve:1.hook: Tang did not look surprised about the missing rice at all.
involve:1.line: 'The audit will *involve* every single item in aisle three — yes, by hand.'

risk:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside. I had forgotten my umbrella, and my shift started in three minutes. I decided to *risk* a sprint through the downpour rather than wait under the bus shelter any longer. I arrived soaked but on time, dripping a small puddle by the door.
risk:1.cnHint: 我决定冒着大雨冲向便利店，结果浑身湿透地准时打卡上班。
risk:1.hook: Then I noticed the stranger watching me from the doorway.
risk:1.line: 'Sometimes you just have to *risk* getting wet,' Tang said, handing me a towel.

success:1.en: The old man outside was doing a little dance in the rain, holding his phone up to the sky. I stepped out to ask if he needed help. He laughed and showed me the screen — his lottery numbers had matched three out of six. Small *success*, he said, but enough for a hot bun.
success:1.cnHint: 老爷爷在雨中欢呼，因为他取得了一点小小的____。
success:1.hook: He bought two buns — one for a person I had not seen yet.
success:1.line: 'A small *success* is still worth dancing for,' he told me cheerfully.

group:1.en: A *group* of students huddled under the store awning, arguing over a shared umbrella that was clearly too small for four people. They were all soaked from the shoulders down. I propped the door open and waved them inside, earning four grateful, dripping smiles and one very muddy doormat.
group:1.cnHint: 一____同学挤在门廊避雨，我把他们请进了店里。
group:1.hook: The last one in quietly slipped a folded note onto the counter.
group:1.line: 'Our whole *group* forgot to check the weather,' the tallest student admitted, laughing.

course:1.en: Lin arrived carrying two coffees and a printout of a new online *course* on convenience-store management. She set one coffee in front of me without a word, then spread the pages across the counter like she owned the place. Outside, rain blurred the streetlights into soft gold coins.
course:1.cnHint: 林走进来，带着一份____资料，悄悄地也给我买了一杯咖啡。
course:1.hook: The course title was circled in red, and my name was written beside it.
course:1.line: 'This *course* might change how we run the night shift,' Lin said quietly.

relationship:1.en: The Manager stood outside in the rain, talking to an elderly woman under her umbrella. They were laughing like old friends. When he finally came in, I asked who she was. He dried his glasses and smiled. 'A long *relationship*,' he said, 'built one cup of tea at a time.'
relationship:1.cnHint: 店长在雨中和一位老奶奶聊天，我好奇他们之间是什么样的____。
relationship:1.hook: He glanced back at her, and something in his eyes looked almost sad.
relationship:1.line: 'A good *relationship* takes years and a lot of tea,' the Manager said softly.

form:1.en: A delivery rider stopped outside and knocked on the glass, holding up a soggy clipboard. He needed me to sign a *form* for a package, but the paper was so wet it tore the moment my pen touched it. We both stared at the sad little heap of pulp and started laughing.
form:1.cnHint: 快递员冒雨送来包裹，让我在一张____上签字，结果纸全湿烂了。
form:1.hook: The package itself was addressed to someone who had never worked here.
form:1.line: 'The *form* is basically soup now,' the rider said, still grinning.

interest:1.en: A boy pressed his nose against the window, staring at the rows of colourful snacks with obvious *interest*. Rain dripped from his hood. I waved him in. He counted coins in his palm very carefully, chose one small bag of crackers, and placed every coin on the counter with quiet dignity.
interest:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩对橱窗里的零食表现出浓厚的____，最后郑重地买下一小包饼干。
interest:1.hook: He pointed at one shelf and whispered a question I almost did not catch.
interest:1.line: 'I have a strong *interest* in that top shelf,' he said very seriously.

simply:1.en: The rain had stopped, but the street was still bright with puddles reflecting the store sign. A woman walked past, paused, turned back, and came inside. She looked around at every corner and then said she had not come to buy anything. She had *simply* wanted to see if the place still felt the same.
simply:1.cnHint: 一位女士走进来，说她____是想看看这家店还是不是原来的感觉。
simply:1.hook: She touched the edge of the counter as though remembering something.
simply:1.line: 'I *simply* needed to stand here for a moment,' she said, almost to herself.

enable:1.en: Rain hammers the street outside. I stand under the store awning, holding an umbrella over an old man sorting through wet bags. The dry shelter I offer seems to *enable* him to find his phone at last. He mutters thanks, punches in a number, and waits. Nobody picks up.
enable:1.cnHint: 我在店门外帮一位老人撑伞，____他终于找到了手机。
enable:1.hook: He dials again, hands shaking more than before.
enable:1.line: 'A little kindness can *enable* a man to keep going, you know.'

simple:1.en: The rain is soft now. A woman stops outside, staring at our handwritten menu board. She tilts her head as if the words are a puzzle. I step out and point to the cheapest item. Her whole face relaxes. Sometimes a *simple* gesture matters more than any words you could say.
simple:1.cnHint: 我用一个____的手势帮助一位看不懂菜单的女士做出了选择。
simple:1.hook: She takes the receipt and reads one line very carefully.
simple:1.line: 'Just point — keep it *simple*, please, I am so tired.'

several:1.en: I am mopping near the door when *several* umbrellas appear at once outside the glass, all bunching up at the entrance. Their owners jostle politely, each waiting for the other to enter first. I count five faces, all damp, all smiling a little. One of them is carrying a large, dripping cardboard box.
several:1.cnHint: 雨中____把雨伞同时挤在门口，大家都礼貌地互相谦让。
several:1.hook: The person with the box hesitates, then looks straight at me.
several:1.line: 'I have visited *several* times, but you are new here, yes?'

struggle:1.en: Outside, a delivery rider tries to tie a torn bag to his bike in the pouring rain. I watch his *struggle* through the window — knot slipping, rain blinding, timer on his phone counting down. I grab a roll of tape from under the counter and run out without thinking.
struggle:1.cnHint: 送餐员在雨中____着捆绑破损的袋子，我冲出去帮忙。
struggle:1.hook: He glances at the tape, then at his screen, and goes very still.
struggle:1.line: 'Every night is a *struggle*, but tonight someone helped — thank you.'

decision:1.en: The rain picks up again. Tang is beside me, watching a young woman pace back and forth under the awning outside, phone pressed to her ear. 'Big *decision*,' Tang says quietly. The woman stops pacing, takes a long breath, and nods to herself. Then she walks away fast, into the dark wet street.
decision:1.cnHint: 一个年轻女人在店门外踱步打电话，阿糖说她在面临重大____。
decision:1.hook: She left something small on the bench outside.
decision:1.line: 'A *decision* made in the rain always feels more real, I think.'

kid:1.en: A *kid* in bright yellow boots splashes into every puddle on the pavement outside, laughing at the sound. His grandmother calls from under a nearby umbrella, pointing at her watch. He ignores her completely, crouches down, and peers at his own reflection in the water with great seriousness.
kid:1.cnHint: 一个穿黄雨靴的____在门外水坑里跳来跳去，完全不理奶奶的催促。
kid:1.hook: Then he looks up and stares directly through our window at me.
kid:1.line: 'Hey mister, every *kid* needs puddles — it is basically a rule.'

ability:1.en: Lin jogs past the window, soaked, balancing four stacked trays of drinks from the rival shop down the street. I have no idea how she moves that fast in the rain without dropping a single cup. That *ability* to stay perfectly steady while everything around her is slipping — I find it honestly impressive.
ability:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林冒雨飞奔，我对她在混乱中保持平稳的____感到由衷佩服。
ability:1.hook: She glances through the glass at me without slowing down at all.
ability:1.line: 'Natural *ability* is fine, but I mostly just practise every single day.'

task:1.en: The Manager calls from inside just as rain begins falling harder. My *task* is simple enough: bring in the folding sign from the pavement before it blows away. I step out, grab the sign, and notice a folded note tucked under its base, held down by a small smooth stone.
task:1.cnHint: 店长交给我一个小____，我出门收招牌时发现了一张神秘纸条。
task:1.hook: The handwriting on the note is oddly familiar.
task:1.line: 'One *task* at a time — that is how we get through the night.'

put:1.en: Rain drums on the shop awning above. I stand outside, about to start my first night shift, and *put* my hand over my name tag to keep it dry. A figure in a yellow coat hurries past, drops something small, and vanishes around the corner before I can call out.
put:1.cnHint: 新来的夜班店员站在门外，把手____在名牌上挡雨，却看见一个黄雨衣的人匆匆跑过，掉落了什么东西。
put:1.hook: The small thing on the wet ground is a phone, still ringing.
put:1.line: 'Just *put* it somewhere dry until the owner comes back.'

difference:1.en: The rain turns the empty street into a mirror. Tang rushes out with an umbrella and stands beside me. 'You will learn,' he says, 'that five minutes of heavy rain makes a big *difference* — every regular shows up wanting hot soup noodles instead of cold tea.' He is already right.
difference:1.cnHint: 同事说，下雨和晴天在顾客需求上有很大的____，这一点我很快就体会到了。
difference:1.hook: Then the door swings open and someone proves him right immediately.
difference:1.line: 'Rain makes a real *difference* to what people want tonight.'

lack:1.en: The street lamp flickers across from the store. I am mopping a puddle that blew in under the door when the Manager steps outside, looks up and down the quiet road, and says our corner gets no business after midnight because of one simple *lack* — there is no bus stop nearby. He sighs.
lack:1.cnHint: 店长站在门外，解释这条街深夜生意差，是因为____一个公交站。
lack:1.hook: Yet right then, headlights sweep the corner and a taxi stops.
lack:1.line: 'The real problem is a *lack* of any bus stop close by.'

case:1.en: A cold wind pushes dead leaves along the pavement. I hold the door open for an old woman carrying a heavy bag. She thanks me and sets the bag down — it turns out to be a worn leather *case* full of sheet music. She is soaked through but smiling, like the rain is no trouble at all.
case:1.cnHint: 一位老太太带着一个装满乐谱的旧____走进来，浑身湿透却笑得从容。
case:1.hook: She asks if the back room has a piano.
case:1.line: 'This old *case* has been with me for forty years, young one.'

sure:1.en: I pull my collar up and step under the awning to wait for Tang to arrive and hand over the store key. The rain is getting heavier and I am not *sure* which entrance staff are supposed to use. A passing cyclist slows, looks at me standing there lost, and laughs kindly before pointing left.
sure:1.cnHint: 我站在店外等同事交接钥匙，却不____该走哪个入口，路过的骑车人笑着指了路。
sure:1.hook: Tang appears from the right, not the left.
sure:1.line: 'Are you *sure* you know which door is the staff entrance?'

enough:1.en: Steam rises from a drain near the kerb. I have just locked my bicycle to a post when I notice a teenage boy sitting on the steps next door, shoulders hunched. He has no umbrella, no hood, no jacket — simply not *enough* clothing for a night this wet. He stares at his shoes.
enough:1.cnHint: 我看到一个少年坐在台阶上，衣服____不够御寒，淋着雨盯着自己的鞋子。
enough:1.hook: He looks up and I realise I have seen his face before.
enough:1.line: 'I did not bring *enough* layers — I thought it would stay warm.'

attention:1.en: The rain eases to a drizzle. A small brown dog sits perfectly still under the bus shelter across the street, and I cannot help watching it. Tang taps my shoulder. 'First rule of this job,' he says with a grin, 'pay *attention* to the store, not to every stray animal on the block.' Fair point.
attention:1.cnHint: 我一直盯着街对面一只迷路的小狗，同事提醒我应该把____放在店里。
attention:1.hook: The dog suddenly stands up and trots straight toward our door.
attention:1.line: 'Pay *attention* to the store first, or the Manager will notice.'

certain:1.en: I am sweeping rain water off the front step when a woman in a grey coat stops under our awning and checks her phone. There is something *certain* in the way she stands — still, unhurried — as if she already knows someone is about to walk around that wet corner to meet her. Nobody comes.
certain:1.cnHint: 一个灰衣女子站在屋檐下，神情____而平静，好像在等一个必会出现的人，但那个人始终没来。
certain:1.hook: Her phone buzzes once, then goes dark.
certain:1.line: 'I am *certain* he said to meet right here at midnight.'

survey:1.en: The rain had just stopped. I stepped outside to *survey* the street before my shift began. Puddles caught the yellow light from the store window. A man in a wet coat stood very still near the corner, staring at the sky as if he was reading something written there.
survey:1.cnHint: 我在班前走出去，____了一下街道的情况，发现角落里站着一个奇怪的人。
survey:1.hook: He hadn't moved in ten minutes.
survey:1.line: 'Let me *survey* the area before we open the side door,' the Manager said.

care:1.en: An old woman came in soaked from the rain. I handed her a small towel from behind the counter. She took it with both hands and thanked me quietly. The Manager watched from the back room and gave me a short nod. Small acts of *care*, he always said, are what keep people coming back.
care:1.cnHint: 一位淋雨的老奶奶走进来，我递给她毛巾，店长说____是留住客人的关键。
care:1.hook: She left a folded note on the counter.
care:1.line: 'Take *care* — the floor near the door is very wet,' I warned her.

state:1.en: Tang arrived late, jacket dripping, breathing hard. 'Bus broke down,' he said. He stood at the counter in a dazed *state*, staring at the coffee machine as if he had forgotten how it worked. I quietly started it for him. He blinked, then smiled. Outside, the rain picked up again.
state:1.cnHint: 阿糖冒雨赶来上班，整个人处于一种恍惚的____，我悄悄帮他把咖啡机打开了。
state:1.hook: His phone buzzed three times — and he ignored all of them.
state:1.line: 'You look like you are in a terrible *state*,' I told Tang.

impact:1.en: A bicycle messenger burst through the door, nearly knocking over the magazine stand. The *impact* of the door hitting the shelf sent three bottles of tea rolling across the floor. He caught two. I caught one. We looked at each other, both breathing fast. 'Sorry,' he said. 'I have a delivery for someone here.'
impact:1.cnHint: 一个送货员冲进来，门撞架子的____让好几瓶茶滚落在地。
impact:1.hook: The name on the delivery tag made me go cold.
impact:1.line: 'The *impact* of that door could break the shelf,' the Manager said firmly.

reason:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street came in and bought nothing — again. She just walked the aisles slowly, eyes moving over every label. There was a *reason* she kept visiting, I was sure of it, but she never said a word. She left the same way she came in: quietly, hood still up.
reason:1.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林又来了什么都不买，只是慢慢逛，我确信她这样做是有____的。
reason:1.hook: Tonight she paused at the storage room door.
reason:1.line: 'There is always a *reason* behind what a person does,' the Manager said quietly.

close:1.en: The rain fell harder around two in the morning. A girl ran under our awning and pressed against the wall, catching her breath. She lived *close* to the store, she said, just half a block away, but the storm had surprised her. She bought a warm can of soup and held it with both hands like a small fire.
close:1.cnHint: 一个女孩躲雨时说她住得离这里很____，但这场暴雨还是让她措手不及。
close:1.hook: She asked if she could stay until the lightning passed.
close:1.line: 'My place is *close* — just past the traffic light,' she said softly.

individual:1.en: Every night person is different. The Manager once told me to pay attention to each *individual* who walks in after midnight — their reasons for being awake are always interesting. A student with paint on her hands. A man carrying a birdcage. A woman who only ever buys salt. Tonight, someone new pushed open the door.
individual:1.cnHint: 店长说要注意每一个深夜来访的____，因为他们各自都有有趣的故事。
individual:1.hook: This one was wearing my old school uniform.
individual:1.line: 'Every *individual* customer matters, even at three in the morning,' the Manager said.

area:1.en: A city worker in an orange vest came in and unrolled a damp map on the counter. He was checking which pipes ran under this *area* of the street. He tapped our block with one finger and frowned. 'There may be some digging next week,' he said. He bought two energy drinks and rolled the map back up.
area:1.cnHint: 一个市政工人进来，展开地图查看这片____的管道情况，说下周可能要施工。
area:1.hook: He hesitated at the door, then turned back to ask one more question.
area:1.line: 'This whole *area* could lose water for a day,' he said, still frowning.

popular:1.en: Rain had been falling all evening. A long line of wet umbrellas stretched outside the store. The Manager stood at the door, watching. 'That new hot drink is so *popular* tonight,' he said, almost to himself. Every customer who passed asked for the same cup. We ran out in an hour.
popular:1.cnHint: 雨夜里，一款热饮突然大受____，店外排起了长队。
popular:1.hook: But the last customer in line only wanted to talk.
popular:1.line: 'That drink is so *popular* that we may never keep enough stock.'

current:1.en: I stepped outside to collect the wet mats. Rain water rushed along the gutter in a fast *current*, carrying a small paper boat someone had folded. A child at the corner watched it go. The Manager called me back inside before I could see where the boat ended up.
current:1.cnHint: 店外水沟里的____把一只纸船冲走了，一个孩子静静地看着。
current:1.hook: The child then looked straight at me and smiled.
current:1.line: 'Watch that *current* — it is stronger than it looks.'

difficult:1.en: Tang and I were restocking shelves before sunrise. The delivery boxes were heavy and the labels were small. 'Reading these tiny numbers is *difficult* in this light,' Tang said, squinting. We had only one working lamp between us. Outside, rain tapped softly on the window like someone asking to come in.
difficult:1.cnHint: 天亮前补货，昏暗的灯光让两人觉得看清标签十分____。
difficult:1.hook: Then Tang found a box that had no label at all.
difficult:1.line: 'It is *difficult* to read anything with only one lamp.'

amount:1.en: The rain brought in a surprising *amount* of customers for a Tuesday night. By two in the morning I had counted over forty people. Most bought hot drinks and stood near the door, watching the street. The Manager seemed pleased but said nothing. He just kept adding numbers in a small notebook.
amount:1.cnHint: 雨夜里来店的顾客____出乎意料地多，店长默默地记着账。
amount:1.hook: One customer had been standing there for over an hour.
amount:1.line: 'The *amount* we sold tonight is more than last week's total.'

point:1.en: Lin arrived just before three, hood dripping, and walked straight to the cold drinks. I could not see the *point* of buying something cold on a night like this. Lin caught my look and grinned. 'Hot weather or cold rain, same answer,' Lin said, holding up a green can. I still did not understand.
point:1.cnHint: 深夜大雨中，隔壁咖啡店的林来买冷饮，叙述者不明白这样做的____在哪里。
point:1.hook: Lin left a folded note under the can on the counter.
point:1.line: 'I do not see the *point* of hot drinks when you are already wet.'

role:1.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me near the entrance while rain blurred the street outside. He said my *role* for the night shift was not just selling things but keeping the store feeling safe and calm. A place where anyone could step in from the dark and breathe. I had not thought of it that way before.
role:1.cnHint: 店长告诉叙述者，夜班的____不只是卖东西，还要让人感到安心。
role:1.hook: Just then, someone knocked on the glass from outside.
role:1.line: 'Your *role* here is to make every person feel welcome.'

suggest:2.en: A folded note sat under the counter, left by someone before my shift. It read: 'The soup by the door sells out fast — I *suggest* you stock twice as much on rainy nights.' No name, no number. Just neat handwriting and a small drawing of an umbrella.
suggest:2.cnHint: 柜台下有人留了一张纸条，____多备些汤。
suggest:2.hook: But the handwriting matched no regular I had ever met.
suggest:2.line: 'I *suggest* you read it before the Manager sees it first.'

improve:2.en: Tang slid a folded checklist across the counter to me. Every row had a note in red pen: 'face the labels forward,' 'wipe the nozzle after each pour.' 'The Manager made this for the last three new clerks,' Tang said. 'It helped them *improve* fast.' The red ink on mine was heavier than I expected.
improve:2.cnHint: 阿糖递来一张清单，说它能帮新人____得很快。
improve:2.hook: The last clerk's name on the list had been crossed out.
improve:2.line: 'Follow this and you will *improve* before the week is over.'

affect:2.en: The rain had been falling since noon, and by midnight the street outside was empty. Tang pointed at the nearly full shelves. 'Weather like this will *affect* everything — foot traffic, hot-drink sales, even our moods.' I nodded and poured two cups of tea. Outside, a lone figure paused under the lamp post.
affect:2.cnHint: 阿糖说这样的天气会____很多事情，包括我们的心情。
affect:2.hook: The figure outside did not carry an umbrella, yet did not come in.
affect:2.line: 'Rain can *affect* sales more than any sale sign ever could.'

support:2.en: A small handwritten sign was taped inside the door: 'Your *support* keeps this little store open — thank you.' The Manager had put it up years ago, Tang told me. Most customers walked past it without looking. But one old man stopped, read it slowly, and gave a small nod before choosing his usual can of warm milk.
support:2.cnHint: 门边贴着一张小告示，感谢大家的____。
support:2.hook: The old man left exact change and a single folded paper crane on the counter.
support:2.line: 'Without your *support*, this corner would just be a dark street.'

hand:2.en: I found a child's drawing tucked behind the magazine rack — a stick figure with a big smile standing behind a counter. In crayon below it: 'the nice *hand* that gave me a sticker.' Tang laughed when she saw it. 'That was the clerk before you. She kept a roll of star stickers in her apron pocket.'
hand:2.cnHint: 杂志架后面藏着一幅画，画的是那只给孩子贴纸的____。
hand:2.hook: The sticker roll was still in the apron hanging on the back hook.
hand:2.line: 'A kind *hand* is remembered longer than any price discount.'

finding:2.en: I was restocking the cold drinks when a folded receipt fell from behind the shelf. On the back, someone had written a list of prices with the note: 'My *finding* — this store is ten cents cheaper than Lin's place across the street on every hot item.' The date at the top was three months old.
finding:2.cnHint: 一张收据背面记录着某人的____：这家店比对面便宜。
finding:2.hook: Lin's store sign flickered once through the rain-streaked window.
finding:2.line: 'That *finding* is why I stopped crossing the street every night.'

ago:2.en: Near the back shelf I noticed a small dent in the wall, painted over but still visible. 'A delivery cart,' Tang said without looking up. 'Two years *ago*, before the Manager re-arranged the whole store.' She said it quietly, as if the dent was a kind of diary entry the wall had kept for itself.
ago:2.cnHint: 墙上的一个凹痕记录着两年____发生的事。
ago:2.hook: Tang's voice went softer when she said the Manager's name just then.
ago:2.line: 'That happened two years *ago*, but the wall still remembers it.'

essay:2.en: Tucked under a bag of chips on the top shelf, I found two pages of neat writing. The header read 'My Neighbourhood — a short *essay*.' A student must have left it by mistake. The opening line was: 'The small store on the corner is the brightest thing on our street after dark.'
essay:2.cnHint: 货架上有人落下了一篇____，第一句话写的是这家店。
essay:2.hook: The student's name on the last page matched a face I had already seen tonight.
essay:2.line: 'I left my *essay* here last week — I thought it was gone forever.'

develop:2.en: The rain tapped the window all night. Around two in the morning, I found an old notebook behind the counter. Inside, someone had drawn a rough map of the neighbourhood and written: 'plan to *develop* this corner into something special.' The handwriting looked familiar. It matched the Manager's exactly.
develop:2.cnHint: 我在柜台后面发现了一本旧笔记本，里面有人写下了____这个街角的计划。
develop:2.hook: The last page had a name crossed out — but I could still read it.
develop:2.line: 'I want to *develop* this little store into the heart of the street,' the Manager once said.

level:2.en: Tang left a sticky note on the cash register before my shift started. It said: 'Shelf three, top row — water got in. Check the *level* of the boxes.' I climbed up and found every box was soaked through. Tucked inside the wettest one was a small sealed envelope with no name on it.
level:2.cnHint: 唐留下便条让我检查货架上积水的____，我却在最湿的箱子里发现了一封信。
level:2.hook: The envelope was sealed, but one corner had already come open.
level:2.line: 'The water *level* on that shelf is way too high — check it tonight,' Tang warned me.

enjoy:2.en: A regular customer came in just after midnight, shaking rain from her coat. She picked up a warm can of corn soup and stood by the heater. 'I *enjoy* these quiet rainy nights,' she said softly, more to herself than to me. She paid, smiled, and left an umbrella by the door — a different one from the one she had carried in.
enjoy:2.cnHint: 一位常客说她____下雨的深夜，但她离开时留下的雨伞和带来的不一样。
enjoy:2.hook: The umbrella she left behind had someone else's name written on the handle.
enjoy:2.line: 'I really *enjoy* the sound of rain when I am warm inside,' she told me quietly.

fact:2.en: Lin came in around three, dripping wet, and bought two bottles of water without a word. I almost missed the *fact* that one bottle had a small folded note tucked under its label. Lin was gone before I could say anything. The note had only four words on it: 'check the back room.'
fact:2.cnHint: 我差点忽视了一个____：林买的水瓶上藏着一张小纸条。
fact:2.hook: I stood at the back-room door for a long moment before I turned the handle.
fact:2.line: 'The *fact* is, I come here every rainy night for a reason,' Lin said once.

news:2.en: The Manager called at four in the morning. The rain was still heavy. 'Any *news* from the night?' he asked. I told him about the wet boxes. He went quiet for a moment, then said, 'Good. Now look under the counter — left side, far back.' I looked. There was a small locked box I had never seen before.
news:2.cnHint: 店长打来电话问夜里有什么____，然后叫我去看柜台下从没注意过的东西。
news:2.hook: The key to the locked box was taped to the back of the phone.

company:2.en: By five in the morning the store was empty and the rain had softened to a whisper. I was glad for the *company* of the little radio on the shelf, playing old tunes no one had chosen. Then I noticed: the radio had no power cord. It was not plugged in anywhere.
company:2.cnHint: 深夜空荡荡的店里，收音机给了我____，但我随后发现了一件奇怪的事。
company:2.hook: The song it played was the same one every hour, without repeating.
company:2.line: 'On a rainy night shift, even a radio is good *company*,' I told myself.

cost:2.en: Tang's note also mentioned that a new stock order had arrived. The total *cost* was printed on the receipt — but someone had drawn a circle around the last item and written a question mark next to it. The item was listed only as 'special order, one unit.' There was no description of what it was.
cost:2.cnHint: 收据上最后一项商品的____旁边有人画了个问号，却没有任何关于它是什么的说明。
cost:2.hook: The special order was not on any shelf I could find.
cost:2.line: 'I do not know what it is, but the *cost* alone tells you it matters,' Tang had written.

idea:2.en: At six the rain finally stopped. Morning light crept through the glass door. I had spent the whole night finding small mysteries and no answers. Then a thought hit me: every odd thing — the notebook, the envelope, the note, the locked box — had turned up on a rainy night. I had an *idea* about who was leaving them. I just needed one more rainy night to be sure.
idea:2.cnHint: 经过一整晚的发现，我有了一个关于是谁留下这些谜题的____，但还需要再等一个雨夜。
idea:2.hook: The next forecast called for heavy rain the following Tuesday.
idea:2.line: 'I have an *idea* who is doing this — and I think they know I know,' I said to myself.

conversation:2.en: Rain tapped the window as I wiped down the counter. An old man came in, shook his umbrella, and bought a can of hot soup. While he waited for his change, he started a quiet *conversation* about the street outside — how it looked forty years ago, how little it had changed. I listened, surprised by how much he remembered.
conversation:2.cnHint: 一位老人在收银台边和我聊起了这条街____年前的样子。
conversation:2.hook: Then he mentioned a name that made me freeze.
