conversation:2.line: 'A good *conversation* is hard to find after midnight,' he said softly.

self:2.en: I found a small notebook wedged behind the lost-and-found box under the counter. Inside the front cover, in neat handwriting, were the words: 'Note to *self* — do not leave this here.' Below that, a list of things someone clearly did not want to forget. The last item on the list was a question, not a task.
self:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了一本笔记本，扉页上写着提醒____的话。
self:2.hook: The question on the last line had no answer written beside it.
self:2.line: 'Note to *self*: always check the lost-and-found,' I muttered.

age:2.en: Tang came in at two in the morning, still wearing her uniform from the day shift. She set a birthday cake box on the counter and sighed. 'It is for the Manager,' she said. 'He never tells anyone his *age*, but Lin found out somehow.' The single candle on the cake was shaped like a question mark.
age:2.cnHint: 阿糖带来了一个生日蛋糕，店长从不告诉别人自己的____。
age:2.hook: Lin arrived a minute later, smiling a little too widely.
age:2.line: 'He never mentions his *age*, so we all just guessed,' Tang said.

future:2.en: A student sat at the corner table for two hours, papers spread around her empty coffee cup. Before she left, she tucked a folded note under the cup. I almost threw it away, but the word 'HELP' on the outside stopped me. Inside, she had written a long question about her *future*, addressed to no one in particular.
future:2.cnHint: 一个学生离开前在桌上留了一张纸条，写满了对自己____的困惑。
future:2.hook: At the bottom she had left a phone number.
future:2.line: 'I just cannot picture my *future* clearly right now,' she had written.

effect:2.en: The Manager hung a small paper sign above the door: 'Rainy nights only — hot drinks half price.' He stood back and studied it with great care. 'Presentation has an *effect* on mood,' he told me seriously, adjusting the sign by one centimetre. Then he bought himself a coffee at half price and looked very pleased.
effect:2.cnHint: 店长贴出了一张雨天特惠告示，说这样做对顾客情绪有____。
effect:2.hook: By midnight, every seat in the store was taken.
effect:2.line: 'A good sign has a real *effect* on people,' the Manager said firmly.

local:2.en: A delivery man came in to escape the rain, dripping on the doormat. He pointed at a handwritten menu card near the register. 'Is that soup *local*?' he asked. I had no idea, so I checked the label on the pot. The brand name was a street two blocks away. He ordered two cups and called someone to share the news.
local:2.cnHint: 一位快递员问我们的热汤是不是____品牌，我去查了标签。
local:2.hook: Whoever he called arrived with an empty thermos ten minutes later.
local:2.line: 'I always prefer something *local* on a cold night,' he said.

tend:2.en: Lin stopped by just before three, holding a damp paper bag. She *tends* to appear at odd hours, the Manager had warned me on my first shift. Tonight she placed the bag on the counter without a word, bought nothing, and stood staring at the rain for a long moment before walking back into the dark street.
tend:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林____在奇怪的时间出现，今晚她放下一个纸袋后一言不发地离开了。
tend:2.hook: The bag was not addressed to anyone, but it had my name on it.
tend:2.line: 'She *tends* to leave things without explaining,' Tang told me later.

term:2.en: I found an envelope taped to the inside of the supply-room door. On it, in the Manager's handwriting: 'End of *term* checklist — read before the rain stops.' Inside was a list of small tasks and, at the very bottom, a short sentence that read more like a warning than a reminder. The rain outside was already slowing down.
term:2.cnHint: 我在储藏室门背后发现了一个信封，上面写着____结束核查清单。
term:2.hook: The last item on the list was crossed out, but still readable.
term:2.line: 'Every *term* ends with that checklist,' Tang said, not meeting my eyes.

risk:2.en: Rain hammered the roof. A wallet lay on the floor near the door, fat with cash. I knew I should lock it in the safe, but I had to *risk* leaving the counter for thirty seconds to reach it. I grabbed it just as the door swung open.
risk:2.cnHint: 我不得不____离开柜台去捡一个装满现金的钱包。
risk:2.hook: The person in the doorway was already staring at my hands.
risk:2.line: 'I had to *risk* it — someone might have grabbed that wallet first.'

success:2.en: Tang slid a handwritten sign across the counter at me. 'Rainy Night Warm Soup — buy one, get one free.' She winked. 'Put it in the window.' By midnight, every cup was gone. She called it a small *success*, but her smile said it felt like something much bigger.
success:2.cnHint: 汤在雨夜推出了一个促销活动，结果出人意料地____。
success:2.hook: Then I noticed she had already written a second sign for tomorrow.
success:2.line: 'A little *success* like this keeps me going on slow nights.'

group:2.en: A *group* of five students burst in out of the rain, laughing and shaking water from their coats. They spread textbooks across the only big table without asking. I brought them a basket of free chopsticks. The quietest one looked up and mouthed a careful thank-you.
group:2.cnHint: 一____学生冲进店里避雨，占了最大的那张桌子。
group:2.hook: One notebook was open to a page with my name written on it.
group:2.line: 'Sorry, can our *group* sit here a little longer? The rain is still heavy.'

relationship:2.en: Lin came in shaking rain from her umbrella. She bought nothing, just studied our shelf layout for ten minutes. I asked if I could help. She said our stores had a 'complicated *relationship*.' Then she took a photo of our new soup sign and walked out into the rain.
relationship:2.cnHint: 林进店不是为了买东西，而是观察我们，还说两家店之间____很微妙。
relationship:2.hook: Her umbrella had our store's logo on it.
relationship:2.line: 'The *relationship* between our two stores is — let's say — interesting.'

form:2.en: A damp envelope sat just inside the door when I arrived. Inside was a single *form*, the kind you fill in to apply for something, with every line already completed in neat handwriting — except for the signature at the bottom. No name. No note. Just rain on the window.
form:2.cnHint: 我到店后发现门口有一封信，里面是一份填好了却没有签名的____。
form:2.hook: The address at the top was this store's address.
form:2.line: 'Did anyone hand in a *form* tonight? It was left by the door.'

interest:2.en: The old man in the corner booth visited every rainy night, always ordering green tea. Tonight he pulled out a small notebook and started sketching the shelves. I watched him, curious. He caught me looking and said his only *interest* at this hour was drawing quiet places. I believed him.
interest:2.cnHint: 角落里的老人告诉我，他深夜来店里的____只有一件事。
interest:2.hook: He turned the notebook around — there was a sketch of me at the counter.
interest:2.line: 'My only *interest* here is tea, silence, and drawing — nothing more.'

simply:2.en: At three in the morning the lights above aisle two began to flicker. I checked the fuse box, checked the bulb, checked the switch. Nothing worked. Tang yawned and said the problem was *simply* that the store was old and tired, just like her. Then both the light and Tang came back on.
simply:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点灯光闪烁，汤____说这不过是老店累了而已。
simply:2.hook: But the fuse box had a sticky note inside that I had never seen before.
simply:2.line: 'It is *simply* an old building — stop looking so worried, new kid.'

reduce:2.en: Rain tapped the window all night. Around 2 a.m., I found a handwritten note taped to the back of the register: 'Turn the music down after midnight. It will *reduce* complaints from the neighbours.' The Manager's handwriting, no doubt — neat and a little bossy. I turned the music down. The street outside looked lonelier than before.
reduce:2.cnHint: 我在收银台后面发现了店长留下的纸条，上面说降低音量可以____邻居的投诉。
reduce:2.hook: But someone had already complained — and left a name.
reduce:2.line: 'It will *reduce* complaints, trust me,' the Manager had written, as if reading my mind.

process:2.en: The rain brought a man in a wet coat who handed me a thick envelope. 'For the Manager,' he said, then left. Inside were printed forms, each page stamped three times. Tang leaned over and whispered that every delivery from that man was part of some long *process* nobody fully understood. I sealed the envelope and put it under the counter, wondering where it would end up.
process:2.cnHint: 唐告诉我，那个送信人每次来都是某个没人完全懂的____的一部分。
process:2.hook: The last form had a name crossed out in red ink.
process:2.line: 'It is part of a long *process*,' Tang said quietly, eyes on the door.

able:2.en: A small parcel had been sitting on the shelf marked 'uncollected' for three weeks — I checked the tag. I tried calling the number on the label twice, but no one answered. Tonight, just before the rain got heavy, I was finally *able* to reach someone. A sleepy voice said, 'Oh, that. Keep it safe, please.' Then the line went dead.
able:2.cnHint: 那个包裹放了三周没人来取，今晚我终于____联系上留下号码的人。
able:2.hook: The voice on the phone did not sound like the name on the label.
able:2.line: 'I was finally *able* to reach you,' I said, but the line had already gone quiet.

drive:2.en: The rain was heavy when a woman ran in, soaking wet, and asked to use our phone. Hers had died. She called someone and said only, 'Don't let the *drive* to finish on time make you take risks on the road.' She hung up, bought a hot drink, and stood watching the rain. She did not look worried. She looked like someone used to waiting.
drive:2.cnHint: 一个浑身湿透的女人跑进来借电话，让对方别因为赶时间的____而在雨天冒险开车。
drive:2.hook: The person she called never called back.
drive:2.line: 'Don't let the *drive* to hurry put you in danger,' she said into the phone, very calm.

face:2.en: Between two bags of rice on the bottom shelf, I found a small photograph someone had left behind — or hidden. A young woman's *face*, smiling, with a date written on the back in pencil: three years ago today. I set it on the counter in case anyone came looking. By morning, it was gone, but I never saw who took it.
face:2.cnHint: 我在货架缝隙里发现了一张照片，上面是某个女人的____，背面写着三年前的今天。
face:2.hook: The pencil date had been lightly erased, then written again.
face:2.line: 'Whose *face* is this?' Tang asked, picking up the photo with one careful finger.

possible:2.en: A regular left his umbrella by the door and walked out into the rain without it. I grabbed it and called after him, but he was gone. I tucked it behind the counter with a sticky note: 'Yours — collect when *possible*.' Tang said he did that every rainy night. Always the same umbrella. Always collected by morning.
possible:2.cnHint: 我给那把落下的伞贴了张便条，说方便的时候来____取走。
possible:2.hook: But this time, morning came and the umbrella was still there.
possible:2.line: 'Collect it when *possible*,' I wrote on the note, pressing it firmly to the handle.

similar:2.en: Lin from the store across the street came in just before three, pretending to browse. She always picks up the same snacks we sell and checks the price tags. Tonight I noticed she had rearranged our shelf display card to face the wall. Her store and ours are *similar* in almost every way — same size, same hours — but she seems to think only one of us will last.
similar:2.cnHint: 林的店和我们的店在规模和营业时间上几乎____，但她好像认为两家只能留一家。
similar:2.hook: She had also swapped the price tag on our best-selling item.
similar:2.line: 'Our stores are *similar*, but mine is tidier,' Lin said, not quite smiling.

involve:2.en: Tang pulled me aside near the storage room and said tonight's late delivery would *involve* signing three forms, not one — something about a new rule the Manager had added without telling anyone. Sure enough, a driver arrived at 3 a.m. with a trolley and a clipboard. I signed all three forms. Tang watched from behind a shelf of instant noodles, nodding slowly like he had seen this before.
involve:2.cnHint: 唐提醒我今晚的收货会____签三份表格，是店长悄悄加的新规定。
involve:2.hook: The third form asked for a signature that was not mine to give.
involve:2.line: 'It will *involve* more paperwork than you expect,' Tang said, already handing me a pen.

put:2.en: The rain had been falling for an hour when an old woman came in and *put* a small envelope on the counter without a word. She just smiled, pulled her coat tight, and walked back out into the wet street. The envelope had my name on it — but I had never seen her before.
put:2.cnHint: 一位陌生老太太把一个信封____在柜台上后悄然离去。
put:2.hook: Inside was a key, still warm.

difference:2.en: Tang showed me how to sort the hot-food shelf during the slow hours. 'Look,' she said, pointing to two rice boxes that looked the same to me. I stared hard and finally saw it — one had a tiny red dot on the lid. 'That *difference* matters,' she said. 'Trust me.'
difference:2.cnHint: 同事指出两个饭盒之间有一个小小的____，让我大开眼界。
difference:2.hook: Then she added, very quietly, 'It matters tonight especially.'
difference:2.line: 'That *difference* is the whole point — look closer.'

lack:2.en: Around two in the morning, a young man came in and stood in front of the snack wall for a long time. He picked things up and put them back. I noticed his hands were shaking a little. It was not a *lack* of money — his wallet was open and full. Something else was missing.
lack:2.cnHint: 深夜，一个年轻人在零食架前久久站着，似乎并非因为____钱。
lack:2.hook: He finally bought a single candle and left without a bag.
lack:2.line: 'It is not a *lack* of money — I just cannot decide.'

case:2.en: The Manager kept a worn notebook under the register. I knocked it off by accident and a photo fell out — a smiling girl standing in front of this very store, years ago. He came over, picked it up without looking at me, and tucked it back in. 'In any *case*,' he said, 'the milk needs restocking.'
case:2.cnHint: 我不小心碰落了店长的笔记本，发现里面藏着一张旧照片，但他只说____如何。
case:2.hook: The girl in the photo looked just like Lin.
case:2.line: 'In any *case*, let us not talk about that now.'

sure:2.en: Lin came in just before three and walked straight to the coffee machine — our coffee machine, the one that belongs to our store. She refilled her cup like she owned the place. I was not *sure* whether to say something or just watch. The Manager, passing by, only nodded at her.
sure:2.cnHint: 竞争对手径直走进来用我们的咖啡机，我完全不____该怎么办。
sure:2.hook: She left two coins on the machine and winked at me.
sure:2.line: 'I am *sure* you do not mind — your manager never does.'

enough:2.en: By four the rain was easing. I had mopped the floor twice, faced every product on the shelves, and counted the change three times. I told myself that was *enough* work for one quiet shift. Then the door opened and a soaking-wet cat walked in and sat down in the middle of the clean floor.
enough:2.cnHint: 我觉得今晚的活已经干得____多了，直到一只猫走进来打破了宁静。
enough:2.hook: It looked at me like it had been waiting for this moment.
enough:2.line: '*Enough* of standing there — someone should dry that cat.'

attention:2.en: I was restacking the drinks cooler when I felt someone watching me. I turned — a small boy, maybe eight, stood at the window pressing his face to the glass. I waved. He did not wave back; his whole *attention* was fixed on the rack of toy keychains near the door, not on me at all.
attention:2.cnHint: 我以为有人在注意我，结果那个小孩的____根本不在我身上。
attention:2.hook: He had been there for twenty minutes, perfectly still.
attention:2.line: 'All my *attention* is on that little star one — please do not move it.'

certain:2.en: Tang handed me a small package that had been left behind the register — no name, no note, just brown paper and string. 'A *certain* regular drops one off every rainy night,' she said, as if that explained everything. She went back to sweeping without another word, and I was left holding it alone.
certain:2.cnHint: 同事说每逢雨夜，____一位常客都会留下一个无名包裹。
certain:2.hook: The package was ticking — very faintly, but ticking.
certain:2.line: 'A *certain* person always comes back for it by morning.'

popular:2.en: A wet Tuesday night, and the store felt sleepy. Then Tang pointed at the snack shelf. 'We sold out of those spicy chips again,' she said. 'They are the most *popular* item we carry. The Manager orders three boxes, but it is never enough.' I looked at the empty hook and wondered who kept buying them all.
popular:2.cnHint: 唐告诉我，某种零食是店里最____的商品，总是卖断货。
popular:2.hook: The next customer walked in, eyes going straight to that empty hook.
popular:2.line: 'Those spicy chips are the most *popular* item in the whole store.'

current:2.en: The rain had knocked out the street light outside. Tang handed me a torch and said, 'Check the back room — the *current* in that circuit trips when it gets wet.' I found the small fuse box behind the mop bucket, flipped the switch, and the light outside blinked back on. Someone had taped a note to the box, but I could not read it yet.
current:2.cnHint: 唐让我去检查后室，因为潮湿天气让那条线路的____出了问题。
current:2.hook: The note on the fuse box was in handwriting I would later recognise.
current:2.line: 'The *current* in that back circuit always trips when it rains.'

difficult:2.en: A customer left a folded paper on the counter before rushing out into the rain. I opened it — a crossword puzzle, half finished, with a note: 'Question 7 is *difficult*. Ask the night clerk.' I had no idea what question 7 was. Tang leaned over, read it, and burst out laughing but would not tell me the answer.
difficult:2.cnHint: 一位顾客留下一张字条，说某道题对他来说太____了，让我来解答。
difficult:2.hook: Tang was still smiling about it an hour after the customer had gone.
difficult:2.line: 'Question seven is just too *difficult* — even I gave up on it.'

amount:2.en: After the rain eased, a man in a wet coat came in and bought every last bottle of sports drink on the shelf. I counted twelve bottles. Tang watched him go and said, 'He does this every storm. I have no idea what he does with that *amount* of drinks.' The Manager's restocking note was already taped to the shelf before the door had even closed.
amount:2.cnHint: 一位常客买走了货架上大____的运动饮料，让我们都很好奇。
amount:2.hook: The Manager seemed to have been expecting exactly this purchase.
amount:2.line: 'I cannot imagine what anyone does with that *amount* of sports drinks.'

point:2.en: Lin appeared at the window, collar up against the rain, and slid a folded receipt under the door. Tang picked it up. 'He circled something,' she said, and passed it to me. A single item was marked with a red dot and a question mark. 'That is his *point*,' Tang said. 'He thinks we priced it wrong.' I checked the shelf tag — and he was right.
point:2.cnHint: 林从窗外递进一张收据，圈出了一处标价，想表达他的____。
point:2.hook: The price error had been there for three weeks and no one had noticed.
point:2.line: 'That is exactly my *point* — the shelf price and the receipt do not match.'

role:2.en: While I was tidying the lost-and-found box, I found an old staff rota with names I did not know — except one: the Manager. Tang glanced at it and said, 'He started as a stock boy, you know. His *role* has changed a lot since then.' She put the rota back without another word, but something in her voice made me curious about what else had changed.
role:2.cnHint: 唐告诉我，店长在这家店里扮演的____与他刚来时大不相同。
role:2.hook: The rota listed one more name that Tang had quietly skipped over.
role:2.line: 'His *role* here has changed more than anyone else in this store.'

survey:2.en: The rain tapped softly against the window as I *surveyed* the shelves during the slow hour before dawn. Every item was in its place — except for a small gap where the hot drinks usually sat. Someone had taken all six cups of instant soup. I checked the log: paid for, every one. But who buys six soups at 3 a.m. in a storm?
survey:2.cnHint: 夜班的我____着货架，发现一个让人好奇的小秘密。
survey:2.hook: The receipt showed one name, written in careful English: Tang.
survey:2.line: 'I always *survey* the shelves at the start of each shift,' I told myself.

care:2.en: A folded note fell out of a returned umbrella left by the door. Inside, in neat handwriting: 'Please give this to the night clerk — with *care*.' Wrapped inside the note was a small packet of ginger sweets, still warm from a coat pocket. I looked out at the rain. Nobody was there.
care:2.cnHint: 一把被归还的雨伞里藏着一个让人心暖的小惊喜，附带着一份____。
care:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like the Manager's.
care:2.line: 'Handle it with *care*,' the note said, 'it matters more than it looks.'

state:2.en: The old radio behind the counter crackled back to life around midnight. Tang had left it unplugged for weeks, saying it only played sad songs. But tonight it hummed just fine. I checked its *state* — dial, wire, speaker — all working. The first song it played was oddly cheerful. Then a voice I did not expect came through the static.
state:2.cnHint: 一台久未使用的收音机突然恢复正常，让我忍不住检查它的____。
state:2.hook: The voice on the radio said my name.
state:2.line: 'Check the *state* of the radio before you throw it out,' Tang had written in the log.

impact:2.en: A heavy box of canned peaches slipped off the top shelf and hit the counter with a loud bang. The *impact* left a small dent in the old wood, but nothing broke. I stared at the dent, heart still jumping. Then I noticed the box had a handwritten label on the bottom: 'For emergencies. Do not open until needed.' I had not put it there.
impact:2.cnHint: 一箱罐头砸在柜台上，留下印记，也留下一个关于那箱东西来历的____。
impact:2.hook: The label was signed with a single letter: L.
impact:2.line: 'The *impact* of that fall could have been much worse,' Lin said later, almost too calmly.

reason:2.en: Lin appeared at the door exactly at 2 a.m., dripping wet, holding a single daisy in a plastic bag. I asked why. Lin paused, looked at the flower, then looked back at me. 'There is a *reason* I come here every rainy night,' Lin said quietly. 'But I will tell you another time.' Then Lin paid for a hot coffee and left without another word.
reason:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在雨夜准时出现，却只给出了一个神秘的____暗示。
reason:2.hook: The daisy had a small note tied to its stem.
reason:2.line: 'There is a *reason* for everything I do — even this,' Lin said with a small smile.

close:2.en: The front door would not lock properly at 4 a.m. I pushed it *close* against the frame again and again, but it kept drifting open an inch. Rain blew in across the welcome mat. I propped a mop against it — the Manager's old trick, Tang had told me. Then someone knocked from outside, quietly, three times.
close:2.cnHint: 雨夜里门关不严实，就在我反复把门____上时，有人在外面轻轻敲门。
close:2.hook: Three knocks, then silence — then three more.
close:2.line: 'Push it *close* and hold it for a second — it sticks in the rain,' Tang had warned me.

individual:2.en: By 3 a.m. the rain had brought in five customers, each with a small wet story. The Manager always said this store was built for the *individual* — one person, one need, one quiet moment at a time. I was starting to understand that. Then I noticed one customer had been standing in the snack aisle for twenty minutes without picking anything up.
individual:2.cnHint: 深夜的顾客各有各的故事，这家店是为每一位____而存在的——直到我注意到那个奇怪的身影。
individual:2.hook: They were reading something hidden behind a bag of crackers.
individual:2.line: 'Every *individual* who walks in here has a reason,' the Manager once said. 'Your job is to notice.'

area:2.en: The rain had flooded the small *area* just outside the back door where we kept the recycling bins. I found this out the hard way — one soggy shoe, cold water up to the ankle. I dragged everything inside and spread old newspapers across the floor to dry. Underneath the last bin, I found a sealed envelope with no name on it.
area:2.cnHint: 暴雨淹没了门外的____，我在清理时发现了一个没有署名的信封。
area:2.hook: The envelope was dated six months ago, the night before the last clerk quit.
area:2.line: 'Keep that *area* clear every night — especially when it rains,' the Manager had said on my first day.

enable:2.en: The rain knocked out the street lights near our store. The Manager pulled a box of spare batteries from under the counter and handed them to me with a calm smile. 'These will *enable* the torch to last all night,' he said. I had not even thought to look for a torch. He had thought of everything.
enable:2.cnHint: 停电后，店长拿出备用电池，____手电筒整晚都能用。
enable:2.hook: But why did he already know the lights would fail tonight?
enable:2.line: 'These will *enable* the torch to last all night,' he said.

simple:2.en: A note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift. The handwriting was neat, the message *simple*: 'Save one meat bun for me. I will be late.' No name, no number. Tang just shrugged and said it happened every week. I saved the bun. I really wanted to know who wrote it.
simple:2.cnHint: 后门贴着一张字条，内容____：给我留一个肉包子。
simple:2.hook: The bun was gone by 3 a.m., taken by a hand I never saw.
simple:2.line: 'The message is *simple* — just save the bun and wait,' Tang said.

several:2.en: I found *several* folded paper cranes sitting on top of the magazine rack, each one tucked between a different issue. Tang told me they had been appearing one by one over the past month. Nobody had seen who left them. I unfolded one carefully and found four small words written inside, in pencil.
several:2.cnHint: 杂志架上藏着____只纸鹤，没人知道是谁放的。
several:2.hook: The four words inside made my hands go very still.
several:2.line: 'I have found *several* of these already — always in the same spot,' Tang said.

struggle:2.en: An old man came in just after midnight, shaking rain from his coat. He stood in front of the instant noodle shelf for a long time, reading every label. His *struggle* to choose was so quiet and serious that I did not interrupt. He finally picked the plainest one, paid without a word, and left a small, tired smile at the door.
struggle:2.cnHint: 一位老人在货架前____了很久，不知道该选哪种泡面。
struggle:2.hook: He came back the next night and stood in the exact same spot.
struggle:2.line: 'The *struggle* to pick just one — I face it every single night,' he said softly.

decision:2.en: A yellow umbrella sat in the lost-and-found basket for three weeks. One rainy Tuesday, two customers reached for it at the same moment and looked at each other. The *decision* was made without a single word: the older one stepped back, the younger one hesitated, then they both started to laugh. They shared it all the way to the corner.
decision:2.cnHint: 两位顾客同时拿起同一把伞，最终做出了一个____。
decision:2.hook: The next morning, two umbrellas sat in the basket instead of one.
decision:2.line: 'That *decision* took one second and made both of us feel better,' the younger one said.

kid:2.en: A small *kid* ran in alone at half past two, shoes soaking wet, holding a crumpled ten-yuan note. She asked, very seriously, for the biggest meat bun we had. I gave her one and she ate it standing at the counter, watching the rain. She said her grandmother was waiting around the corner. I hoped that was true.
kid:2.cnHint: 一个____深夜独自跑进店里，认真地买了一个最大的肉包子。
kid:2.hook: She left before I could ask which corner she meant.
kid:2.line: 'I am not a little *kid* — I know exactly what I want,' she said firmly.

ability:2.en: Tang had the *ability* to read a customer's mood before they even reached the counter. She would already have the right change ready, or quietly move a chair closer, or simply not talk. I watched her do it for an hour on that rainy night and tried to take notes. She caught me and just said, 'You will learn.'
ability:2.cnHint: 阿糖有一种特殊的____，能在顾客开口之前就察觉到他们的心情。
ability:2.hook: She never once explained how she knew — and that was the whole lesson.
ability:2.line: 'The *ability* to read people — that is the real job here,' Tang said quietly.

task:2.en: The Manager left me a handwritten list before he went home: restock the top shelf, check the dates on the bread, write down any customer who came in after 3 a.m. That last *task* felt oddly specific. I kept the notebook ready all night. Only one person came in after three, and they bought nothing — just stood, looked around, and left.
task:2.cnHint: 店长留下的清单里，最后一项____让我觉得有些奇怪。
task:2.hook: The person's face was turned away from the camera the whole time.
task:2.line: 'Your last *task* tonight is to write down everyone who comes in after three,' the Manager said.

course:2.en: A damp envelope sat on the back shelf, unclaimed for three nights. Inside, I found a printout — a sign-up sheet for an online *course* in cake decoration, with Tang's name written at the top in careful letters. Someone had clearly left it here on purpose.
course:2.cnHint: 唐在便利店的货架上发现了一封信，里面是一张关于____的报名表。
course:2.hook: But the second name on the list made my heart jump.
course:2.line: 'I signed up for this *course* weeks ago — why is it still here?'
